2611.03647.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
2611.03647.abstract: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi
2611.03647.comment: Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

llm.title_ja: Pixel-UMI: センサー付きの人のデモンストレーションから環境認識型全身マニピュレーションを学習する
llm.tldr_ja: 人のデモンストレーションから環境認識型の全身マニピュレーションポリシーを学習するパイプライン「Pixel-UMI」を提案し、5つの困難なタスクで平均87.0%のタスク達成度を記録した。
llm.problem: 体格の違いがポリシー学習を複雑にし、残余姿勢誤差による視点ミスマッチが生じる。
llm.method: 環境認識型リターゲット（EAR）、リターゲット誤差考慮型マスキング（REAM）、およびDAggerによる人による修正の収集を用いる。
llm.result: 5つの困難なタスクで平均87.0%のタスク達成度を達成した。

2611.03648.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
2611.03648.abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

llm.title_ja: Pixel: 汎用モバイルマニピュレーション学習のための共同設計されたフルスタックロボットシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 汎用モバイルマニピュレーション学習に向けて、ハードウェア、データ収集、全身制御、ポリシー学習を統合した共同設計フルスタックシステム「Pixel」を提案する。
llm.problem: コンポーネントが個別に開発されるためミスマッチが生じ、システム全体の能力が制限される。
llm.method: 低コストの車輪型ヒューマノイド、多様なデータ収集インターフェース、統合された全身コントローラー、共通のポリシー学習パイプラインを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 器用さ、能動知覚、ナビゲーション、全身協調を必要とするモバイルマニピュレーション動作を実証した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.03646.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
2611.03646.abstract: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.

llm.title_ja: EgoActionBench: 視点映像に対する密なアクションキャプションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 連続する人のマニピュレーションを時間的に局所化したアトミックアクションとして表現するベンチマーク「EgoActionBench」を導入し、20のベースラインモデルを評価した。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークはアクションの原子性、時間的精度、手の動作の関連付けにおいて限界がある。
llm.method: 左手、右手、または両手に紐づく時間的に局所化されたアトミックアクションのアノテーションを含むデータセットを構築し、評価プロトコルを提案する。
llm.result: 既存モデルにはアクションの原子性や時間的精度、手の関連付けに重大な限界があることが明らかになった。

2611.03622.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
2611.03622.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

llm.title_ja: D&A: 記述と評価の分離によりVLMをゼロショットのロボット報酬モデルとして活用する
llm.tldr_ja: シーンダイナミクスを客観的に記述するフェーズと明確な基準で評価するフェーズに分離する手法「D&A」により、VLMのゼロショット進捗推定の確認バイアスを緩和する。
llm.problem: VLMのゼロショット進捗推定は、確認バイアスやハルシネーションに苦しんでおり、非線形な進捗や失敗を捉えられない。
llm.method: タスクに根ざしたシーンダイナミクスの客観的テキスト記述と、明示的な評価基準を用いた評価フェーズに分離する。
llm.result: ゼロショット推定を調整し、確認バイアスを緩和して、失敗を適切にペナルティしつつ成功を補間する微細な進捗メトリクスを提供した。

2611.03617.title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
2611.03617.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

llm.title_ja: 大規模言語モデルの科学的発見能力のトレーニングデータへのトレーシング
llm.tldr_ja: トレーニングセット内のモノファクト（一度だけ観測された事実）の割合が、オープンウェイトモデルの科学的発見能力を決定する鍵であることを理論的・実験的に示した。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルの信頼性の高い科学的発見を可能にする要因について基本的な疑問が残されている。
llm.method: トレーニングセットにおけるモノファクトの割合を直接操作し、複数のオープンウェイトモデルファミリー等で発見数を検証する。
llm.result: より多くのモノファクトが一貫して多くの発見をもたらし、トレーニングデータのモノファクト率が発見を左右する主要因であることを特定した。

2611.03595.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
2611.03595.abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries. We study dynamic-boundary 4D CFD prediction for articulated moving geometries and introduce RoboCFD-4D, a temporally resolved robotic CFD benchmark spanning diverse morphologies and flow conditions. To address the computational and autoregressive challenges of this setting, we propose DynaSolver, a neural operator that explicitly conditions on boundary evolution and causal flow history. DynaSolver employs an efficient physical-token formulation that amortizes point-to-token projection across the operator stack, substantially reducing repeated point-space spatio-temporal computation while retaining accurate point-level reconstruction. We further introduce Replay-Augmented Parallel Training, which exposes the model to autoregressively generated histories while preserving parallel dense supervision, narrowing the gap between ground-truth-conditioned training and autoregressive rollout. Experiments on RoboCFD-4D show that DynaSolver achieves the best full-rollout accuracy among a broad range of learned CFD surrogates, with its advantage increasing as rollout proceeds, indicating substantially reduced autoregressive error accumulation. Project page: https://made-gpt.github.io/DynaSolver-ProjectPage.

llm.title_ja: DynaSolver: 動的境界を持つ自己回帰的4D流体予測のためのニューラルオペレーター
llm.tldr_ja: 連続的に動く境界によって引き起こされる非定常流をモデル化するニューラルオペレーター「DynaSolver」を提案し、動的境界4D CFD予測の精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: 従来のニューラルオペレーターは静的ジオメトリ用に設計されており、動的境界を持つ流れをモデル化できない。
llm.method: 境界の進化と因果的流体履歴を明示的に条件付けするニューラルオペレーターと、物理トークン定式化を採用する。
llm.result: RoboCFD-4Dにおいて学習済みCFD代替モデルの中で最高のフルロールアウト精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルオペレーター

2611.03588.title: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition
2611.03588.abstract: Robust 3D point-cloud recognition is critical for robotics, mapping, and urban sensing, yet point-cloud classifiers often suffer performance drops under domain shifts caused by sensor changes, environmental variation, and acquisition artifacts. Many existing adaptation methods are difficult to deploy in practice because they require access to source data or the internal parameters of the source model, which may be restricted by privacy, licensing, or security constraints. We present 3D-BBDA, a backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation framework that adapts a source-trained predictor to unlabeled target data using only black-box outputs. Our method performs pseudo-label guided prototype-based alignment and employs a weighted prediction module to fuse source logits with alignment logits, reducing sensitivity to noisy pseudo-labels. To stabilize prototype memory when pseudo-label coverage is incomplete, we construct a Gaussian-perturbed prototype prior from unlabeled target predictions and use it as a fallback for missing or unreliable class prototypes during alignment. Experiments on four corrupted 3D benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines. On ModelNet-40C, 3D-BBDA achieves mean errors of 32.08% (PointNet) and 29.62% (GDANet), outperforming Source-only (35.88% / 34.03%) and BFTT3D (33.78% / 32.36%). 3D-BBDA requires only a single forward pass with no gradient updates making it suitable for real-time, privacy-preserving deployment in transferable 3D recognition pipelines. Project page is available at https://visdomlab.github.io/3D_BBDA

llm.title_ja: 3D-BBDA: ロバストな3D点群認識のための逆伝播不要ブラックボックスドメイン適応
llm.tldr_ja: ソースデータの内部パラメータにアクセスせず、ブラックボックス出力のみを用いて教師なしターゲットデータに適応するフレームワーク「3D-BBDA」を提案した。
llm.problem: プライバシー、ライセンス、セキュリティの制約により、ソースデータや内部パラメータへのアクセスが制限される。
llm.method: 擬似ラベル誘導型プロトタイプベースの整合と、ソースロジットと整合ロジットを融合する重み付き予測モジュールを用いる。
llm.result: ModelNet-40Cなどの4つの破損3Dベンチマークで一貫した性能向上を実証した。

2611.03584.title: TAMPAgent: Agentic Belief-Space Planning for Mobile Manipulation
2611.03584.abstract: Open-world robotic mobile manipulation requires acting in physical environments with only partial information. While recent Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) agents show strong open-world reasoning capabilities, existing architectures that rely on direct tool calling struggle with geometric uncertainty and thus are limited to fully-observable tabletop environments. In contrast, Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) systems can solve long-horizon tasks under partial observability but incur high computational costs and require closed worlds. We propose \textbf{TAMPAgent}, an agentic planning framework that unifies the reasoning of LVLMs with the structured constraint satisfaction of TAMP systems. We endow an LVLM agent with a belief-space planning model operating over an extensible API of perception, planning, and control tools. The agent formulates a partial task plan composed of parameterized observation and execution actions, which is subsequently completed using classical search algorithms. After extracting the plan's geometric constraints, the agent leverages its tool API to bind valid parameter values, satisfying feasibility requirements and producing an executable motion plan. Upon execution, the agent continuously updates its belief history and repeats this closed-loop process by interleaving observation and manipulation actions. Evaluated across complex household mobile manipulation tasks on Rainbow Y1 and Unitree G1 platforms, TAMPAgent significantly outperforms direct tool-calling agentic baselines, demonstrating that integrating TAMP constraint satisfaction into agentic planning loops is essential for unstructured, partially observable environments.

llm.title_ja: TAMPAgent: モバイルマニピュレーションのためのエージェント型信念空間計画
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模ビジョン言語モデル（LVLM）のエージェントの推論とTAMPシステムの制約充足を統合したエージェント型計画フレームワーク「TAMPAgent」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のLVLMエージェントは幾何学因果関係の不確実性に苦しみ、完全観測可能な卓上環境に限定されている。
llm.method: 感知、計画、制御ツールの拡張可能API上で動作する信念空間計画モデルをLVLMエージェントに装備する。
llm.result: 家庭内モバイルマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、直接ツール呼び出し型のエージェントベースラインを大きく上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.03585.title: Seeing Through the Illusion: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models
2611.03585.abstract: World action models (WAMs) jointly generate actions and imagined futures, but a plausible prediction need not be realized by its co-generated action. We introduce WISE (\emph{World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation}), a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled rollout on action validity and temporal regularity, inverse-dynamics consistency between the proposed action and the imagined motion, and instruction-conditioned task progress, and executes the highest-scoring candidate while keeping the WAM frozen. With four candidates per decision, WISE raises closed-loop success from 6.0\% to 24.0\% on RoboLab with Cosmos~3 Edge and from 75.1\% to 78.3\% mean success on LIBERO with DreamZero, and exceeds the best existing selector in aggregate by 4.0 and 0.9 points. Component ablations and agreement analyses show that the three scores rank candidates differently and that task progress carries the largest weight in the fused decision.
2611.03585.comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on From Generative Models to Robot Actions (G2A)

llm.title_ja: 幻影を通して見る: 世界行動モデルのためのテスト時スケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 世界行動モデル（WAM）のサンプリングされたロールアウトを評価・選択する事前実行セレクター「WISE」を提案し、閉ループの成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルは妥当な予測を生成するが、もっともらしい予測が必ずしも対応する行動によって実現されるとは限らない。
llm.method: 行動の妥当性、時間的規則性、逆動力学の整合性、タスクの進捗に基づいて各ロールアウトをスコアリングし、最良の候補を実行する。
llm.result: RoboLabやLIBEROにおいて閉ループの成功率を大きく向上させ、既存の最良セレクターを上回った。
keywords_ja: テスト時スケーリング

2611.03548.title: Mediating Human-Swarm Interactions Through a Robot Helper: A Shepherding-Inspired Approach
2611.03548.abstract: This work investigates human-swarm interaction (HSI) for steering large collectives through an intermediary robot helper. While prior robot-swarm control and HSI techniques commonly assume swarm members are addressable, these assumptions often fail for ``ungovernable'' swarms such as wildlife flocks and schools of fish. Motivated by pastoral shepherding, we compare low-level teleoperation to a higher-autonomy motion-primitives interface in a virtual reality (VR) shepherding task under varied swarm cohesion dynamics. Results indicate that motion primitives that operate on collective shape (e.g., boundary-based control) improve task performance and reduce perceived workload.

llm.title_ja: ロボットヘルパーを通した人間と群れの相互作用の仲介: 牧羊にインスパイアされたアプローチ
llm.tldr_ja: 仲介役のロボットヘルパーを用いて大規模な群れを誘導する人間と群れの相互作用（HSI）を調査し、集合の形状に基づくモーションプリミティブがタスク性能を向上させることを示した。
llm.problem: 野生の鳥の群れや魚の群れなど、制御不可能な群れに対して従来の群れ制御やHSI手法は適用できない。
llm.method: 牧羊にインスパイアされ、低レベルのテレオペレーションと、群れの集合形状を操作する高自律なモーションプリミティブインターフェースを比較する。
llm.result: 集合形状を操作するモーションプリミティブが、タスク性能を向上させ、知覚される作業負荷を軽減することを示した。
keywords_ja: 人間とロボットの協調
モーションプリミティブ

2611.03520.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
2611.03520.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion. To provide these complementary sensing capabilities, we present PanoTac, a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip designed for dense three-axis tactile sensing. Each fingertip provides a $12 \times 32 \times 3$ tactile representation, with one normal ($z$) and two shear ($x$, $y$) response components at each taxel. The sensor operates at 60 Hz and costs less than $50 per fingertip. Sensor characterization quantifies response repeatability and consistency across sensor instances and contact locations. We integrate PanoTac into a robotic system with a visuo-tactile pipeline. Across test-tube preparation, grain scooping, and salt pouring, the resulting policies outperform vision-only baselines by an average of 46.7 percentage points. Ablations show that removing either spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces overall performance across the task suite. Our project page is available at https://panotac.github.io.

llm.title_ja: PanoTac: ロバストな触覚中心マニピュレーションのための高密度3軸触覚センサー
llm.tldr_ja: 詳細な接触ジオメトリと相互作用力を捉える低コストで柔軟な3軸触覚センサー「PanoTac」を開発し、視覚のみのベースラインを大幅に上回る性能を実証した。
llm.problem: 接触の豊かなマニピュレーションには接触ジオメトリと力の両方を捉える触覚フィードバックが必要である。
llm.method: 12×32×3の触覚表現を持つ低コストで柔軟な触覚指先を開発し、視覚触覚パイプラインに統合する。
llm.result: 試験管の準備、穀物のすくい上げ、塩の注ぎにおいて、視覚のみのベースラインを平均46.7ポイント上回った。
llm.limitation: 要旨 in 記載なし
keywords_ja: 触覚マニピュレーション

2611.03501.title: When Robots Outweigh Objects: How Inertia Mismatch Shapes Robot Policy Learning
2611.03501.abstract: Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless demonstrated a wide range of successful manipulation behaviors on these platforms, suggesting that even extreme inertia mismatch can be overcome with sufficient data. However, it remains unclear whether high inertia imposes a hidden cost on learning, potentially worsening scaling with data or lowering the performance ceiling of modern robot learning methods. We investigate this question through controlled simulation experiments that vary robot and object masses. We find that reinforcement learning succeeds across a broad range of mass combinations, while behavior cloning learns more reliable policies when a lighter robot manipulates a heavier object, and more data narrows the resulting gap without closing it. Behavior cloning likewise degrades on a simulated robot arm as its motors reflect more inertia through their gearing, even though its weight stays the same. Finally, because new hardware is rarely an option, we explore ways to lower contact inertia on the arm one already has, either by choosing a lower-inertia workspace before collecting data or by steering the demonstrator toward lower-inertia solutions of the task. In both simulated cases, the lower-inertia demonstrations are imitated more reliably. Project website: https://younghyopark.me/inertia-mismatch/

llm.title_ja: ロボットが物体を上回る時: 慣性のミスマッチがロボットのポリシー学習をどのように形作るか
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットと物体の質量を変化させたシミュレーション実験を通じて、極端な慣性ミスマッチがロボットのポリシー学習に与える隠れたコストを調査した。
llm.problem: 重いロボットアームが軽い物体を操作する際、接触時に大きな慣性ミスマッチが生じ、物体を弾き飛ばしてしまう。
llm.method: ロボットと物体の質量を変化させた制御されたシミュレーション実験により、強化学習と行動模倣の挙動を検証する。
llm.result: 行動模倣は軽いロボットが重い物体を操作する時により信頼性の高いポリシーを学習し、低慣性のデモンストレーションほど容易に模倣できることを示した。

2611.03498.title: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
2611.03498.abstract: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

llm.title_ja: SNAP: 歩行者の中でのセマンティックナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的な人間状態の推定に頼らず、単一のセマンティック注釈付き鳥瞰図（BEV）マップからセマンティック地形と動的障害物を同時に推論する強化学習ナビゲーションポリシーを提案した。
llm.problem: 混雑した都市環境をナビゲートする際、群れの回避とセマンティックな経路計画が個別に扱われがちである。
llm.method: 単一のセマンティックBEVマップを用いてセマンティック地形と動的障害物を同時に推論する強化学習ポリシーを構築し、脚式ロボットにゼロショット移行する。
llm.result: 既存の群れナビゲーションおよびセマンティック認識ベースラインを上回り、脚式ロボットへのゼロショット移行に成功した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックナビゲーション

2611.03490.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
2611.03490.abstract: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.
2611.03490.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

llm.title_ja: リプシッツ定数を使わない過駆動マルチローター配分のための遅延保証即応性バリア
llm.tldr_ja: 速度コントローラーの遅延やサンプリングに対応し、リプシッツ定数を必要とせずに過駆動マルチローターの即応性を保証するテストを提案した。
llm.problem: 過駆動マルチローターにおいて、サンプリングされたコマンドと可変な速度コントローラーの遅延により、頑健性のBoundsが非常に小さくなる。
llm.method: 各ローターの単調かつ閉形式の応答特性を利用し、切り替え時間下で到達可能な速度を安価なボックスとして計算する。
llm.result: ヘキサローターのシミュレーションにおいて、遅延やジッターがある場合でも安全バリアの違反を引き起こさなかった。

2611.03489.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
2611.03489.abstract: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

llm.title_ja: ロボットマニピュレーションに向けた近接・触覚センシングの探索
llm.tldr_ja: 3つのマルチゾーンToFセンサーと光学式圧力センサーアレイを組み合わせたマルチモーダル触覚センサー「ToFTouch」を開発し、把持前調整や狭い空間への挿入等での有用性を実証した。
llm.problem: 接触前の情報を取得する事前接触センシングのロボットハンドへの応用やその検証が求められている。
llm.method: 3つのマルチゾーンToFセンサーと光学式圧力センシングアレイを組み合わせたマルチモーダル触覚センサーをパラレルジョーグリッパーに搭載する。
llm.result: ToFフィードバックにより、把持前調整のサイクルタイム短縮や、クラッタからのアイテム抽出、狭所への挿入精度向上が実現できた。

2611.03446.title: Clinician-AI Collaboration in Endovascular Neurointerventions: In-Vitro User Study of Copilot Assistance Modes for Robotic Navigation Across the Autonomy Spectrum
2611.03446.abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an effective treatment for acute ischemic stroke, yet access remains limited by the availability of neurointerventional expertise. Telerobotic and AI-assisted systems may help address this challenge, but it remains unclear how clinicians interact with different levels of autonomy and how autonomous navigation systems perform in realistic environments. This work introduces Copilot Assistance Modes (CAMs), a framework for clinician-AI collaboration in robotic endovascular navigation spanning the autonomy spectrum from manual operation to full autonomy. In the first in-vitro user study comparing clinician-AI collaboration strategies, 11 experts and two students evaluated six navigation modes in a patient-specific vascular phantom. Objective performance metrics were combined with subjective assessments, including workload and usability. Autonomous performance was additionally evaluated both in silico and in vitro to investigate sim-to-real transfer. Hands-on manual navigation achieved the strongest overall performance (100% success). While fully autonomous navigation achieved 81% success in simulation, performance dropped to 23% in vitro. In contrast, several clinician-AI shared-autonomy modes achieved success rates of 92-97%, approximately four times higher than full autonomy and comparable to direct robotic control (95%), demonstrating mitigation of sim-to-real domain shift through clinician-AI collaboration. Among the evaluated AI-driven approaches, user-directed task delegation and rotational shared control demonstrated the most favorable balance between performance and clinician acceptance. These findings suggest that effective clinician-AI collaboration and allocation of control authority may currently be more important for reliable robotic neurointerventional navigation than increasing autonomy alone.

llm.title_ja: 血管内神経治療における臨床医とAIの協調: 自律性のスペクトラムにわたるロボットナビゲーションのコパイロット支援モードの体外使用者調査
llm.tldr_ja: 手動操作から完全自律までの自律性スペクトラムにわたる臨床医とAIの協調フレームワーク「CAMs」を提案し、体外ファントムを用いたユーザー調査を実施した。
llm.problem: 急性虚血性脳卒中の機械的血栓回収術において治療へのアクセスが限られており、臨床医が様々なレベルの自律性とどう協調するか不明確である。
llm.method: 手動から完全自律までの6つのナビゲーションモードを評価する、11人の専門家と2人の学生による体外使用者調査を実施する。
llm.result: 臨床医とAIの共有自律モードは、完全自律に比べ約4倍高い92〜97%の成功率を達成し、ドメインシフトを軽減できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 血管内ナビゲーション

2611.03430.title: Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation
2611.03430.abstract: Autonomous mobility is essential for sustained lunar surface operations, as communication delays and line-of-sight occlusions limit continuous teleoperation. Although recent traversability estimation methods increasingly rely on deep learning, the domain gap between terrestrial analogue environments and real lunar terrain can limit their generalisation, and real lunar traversability labels are scarce, making fully supervised training difficult. To address these challenges, we build a weakly supervised framework trained on sparse pairwise annotations and study whether augmenting visual features with depth-derived geometric information: depth, surface normals, and combined geometric descriptors. We evaluate the models in both in-domain and cross-domain settings using two terrestrial analogue datasets and the real lunar Chang'E PCAM dataset. Contrary to expectations, we find that naive geometric augmentation yields no consistent improvement over a strong visual-only baseline in either setting, with effects small relative to seed-to-seed variance. Instead, the choice of training source emerges as the dominant factor in transfer quality: models trained on domain-relevant sources transfer substantially better to real lunar imagery than the geometric fusion strategy improves any single model. Our evaluation runs onboard a resource-constrained edge device and provides a controlled baseline for designing more expressive multimodal fusion architectures in future lunar perception systems.

llm.title_ja: クロスデータセット月面走行可能性推定のための深度拡張視覚特徴の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 疎なペアワイズアノテーションで訓練された弱教師ありフレームワークを構築し、深度由来の幾何学的情報の追加が月面走行可能性推定の汎化性能に与える影響を評価した。
llm.problem: 地球のアナログ環境と実際の月面地形の間のドメインギャップが汎化を制限し、実際の月面走行可能性ラベルが不足している。
llm.method: 深度、法線、幾何学的記述子などの深度由来の幾何学的情報を視覚特徴に統合し、複数のデータセットでモデルを評価する。
llm.result: 素朴な幾何学的拡張は一貫した性能向上をもたらさず、データセットの選択が転移品質の支配的要因であることが判明した。

2611.03428.title: Toward Uncertainty-Aware, Physics-Grounded Human World Models
2611.03428.abstract: A robot that acts around people needs a world model of the human: a belief over the person's body state and a dynamics model that predicts where that state goes next. This abstract argues that two published components form exactly these two halves, and specifies how to couple them. KNOWN [1] reconstructs the 3D human body while estimating both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in real time (11.6 ms per frame); its aleatoric term identifies unreliable observations, its epistemic term identifies inputs from low-density regions of the training data, and refinement driven by the epistemic term reduces the error on such inputs from 81.3 to 70.3 mm. PhysMoP [2] predicts future body configuration by solving the Euler-Lagrange equations of the body with learned dynamics terms, reducing the 80 ms prediction error from 9.6 to 2.1 mm on Human3.6M and from 12.1 to 0.7 mm on 3DPW. We define the interface between the two, propose three mechanisms by which KNOWN's uncertainty enters PhysMoP, and specify an evaluation protocol on in-the-wild video. No new experimental results are reported here.

llm.title_ja: 不確実性を考慮した物理ベースの人間世界モデルに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 人の3D身体再構築を行うKNOWNと物理ベースの挙動予測を行うPhysMoPの2つのコンポーネントを結合し、不確実性を考慮した物理ベースの人間世界モデルのインターフェースと評価プロトコルを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットが人の周りで行動するためには、人の身体状態の信念とそのダイナミクスを予測する人間世界モデルが必要である。
llm.method: KNOWNが提供する不確実性をPhysMoPのダイナミクス予測に組み込む3つのメカニズムとインターフェースを定義する。
llm.result: 新しい実験結果は報告されておらず、モデルの統合方法、インターフェースの提案、および評価プロトコルの策定を行った。
llm.limitation: 新しい実験結果は報告されていない

2611.03418.title: Myoelectric Control for Upper-Limb Exoskeletons: A Decoder-Shaper-Controller Framework, Design Guidelines, and Future Directions
2611.03418.abstract: Myoelectric Control Systems (MCSs) enable voluntary control of wearable robots through muscle activity. However, intention decoding, assistance shaping, and low-level actuator control are often not explicitly distinguished, making their contributions difficult to evaluate and compare. This review introduces a functional decoder-shaper-controller framework for continuous myoelectric control of upper-limb exoskeletons. The decoder estimates an intention-related variable from surface electromyography (sEMG), the shaper maps it to a control reference according to an assistance policy, and the controller realizes that reference through actuator control. This decomposition separates intention estimation from assistance-policy design and enables comparison of heterogeneous architectures. Representative approaches are critically examined in terms of module design, calibration, and evaluation. The analysis highlights that the shaper, despite determining the magnitude and shape of assistance, lacks established design and tuning methodologies and is often embedded within the decoder or controller. Key open issues include inconsistent reporting of assistance levels, limited use of interaction-aware stability and passivity tools, and insufficient validation across degrees of freedom, users, and tasks. Building on these findings, this review provides design guidelines for systematic module-wise tuning and identifies future research priorities to bridge the gap between accurate intention decoding and safe, effective, and generalizable assistance under real-world operating conditions.

llm.title_ja: 上肢外骨格のための筋電制御: デコーダー・シェーパー・コントローラーフレームワーク、設計指針、および今後の方向性
llm.tldr_ja: 上肢外骨格の連続的な筋電制御に向けた機能的デコーダー・シェーパー・コントローラーフレームワークを提案し、モジュール設計や今後の研究課題を総括した。
llm.problem: 意図のデコード、アシストのシェーピング、低レベルの駆動制御が明確に区別されておらず、貢献の評価や比較が困難である。
llm.method: 表面筋電図（sEMG）からの意図推定、制御リファレンスへのマッピング、アクチュエーター制御への分解によるフレームワークを導入し、従来手法を分析する。
llm.result: シェーパーの設計手法の欠如や、アシストレベルの報告の不統一などの課題を明らかにし、系統的なモジュール別チューニングのための設計指針を提供した。
keywords_ja: ウェアラブルロボット

2611.03410.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
2611.03410.abstract: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

llm.title_ja: OpenZilo: ロボットとの人間中心のセンシングと相互作用のためのオープン・スマートリングプラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: マイク、IMU、PPG、体温センサーを統合したオープン・スマートリングプラットフォーム「OpenZilo」を提案し、音声とジェスチャーによるロボット操作を評価した。
llm.problem: ウェアラブルロボットインターフェースは、ユーザーの入力をタイムリーな物理的行動に接続する必要があるが、その統合的な研究プラットフォームが不足している。
llm.method: 音声およびジェスチャー認識機能を持つスマートリングを構築し、データ収集、イベント解釈、相互作用ポリシー、ロボット実行を分離したソフトウェアアーキテクチャを実装する。
llm.result: 音声とジェスチャー制御のタスク成功率がそれぞれ90.4%と88.8%に達し、ウェアラブルインターフェースとしての有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: ウェアラブルデバイス
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.03350.title: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning
2611.03350.abstract: Robust machine learning for graph-structured data has made significant progress against test-time attacks, yet certified robustness to poisoning - where adversaries manipulate the training data - remains largely underexplored. For image data, state-of-the-art poisoning certificates rely on partitioning-and-aggregation schemes. However, we show that these methods fail when applied in the graph domain due to the inherent label and structure sparsity found in common graph datasets, making effective graph-partitioning difficult. To address this challenge, we propose a novel semi-supervised learning framework called deep Self-Training Graph Partition Aggregation (ST-GPA), which enriches each graph partition with informative pseudo-labels and synthetic edges, enabling effective certification against node-label and graph-structure poisoning under sparse conditions. Our method is architecture-agnostic, scales to large numbers of partitions, and consistently and significantly improves robustness guarantees against both label and structure poisoning across multiple benchmarks, while maintaining strong clean accuracy. Overall, our results establish a promising direction for certifiably robust learning on graph-structured data against poisoning under sparse conditions.
2611.03350.comment: Published at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) 2026

llm.title_ja: ラベルおよび構造ポイズニングに対するグラフニューラルネットワークの認証
llm.tldr_ja: グラフ構造データにおけるトレーニングデータのポイズニングに対し、疑似ラベルと合成エッジを用いた新しい半教師あり学習フレームワークST-GPAにより、スパースな条件下でも効果的な頑健性認証を実現した。
llm.problem: グラフデータにおけるラベルおよび構造のスパース性のため、既存のポイズニング認証手法が適用できない。
llm.method: グラフの各パーティションに疑似ラベルと合成エッジを付与する深層自己学習グラフパーティション集約フレームワーク（ST-GPA）の提案。
llm.result: 複数のベンチマークにおいて、クリーンな精度を維持しながら、ラベルおよび構造ポイズニングに対する頑健性保証を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: グラフニューラルネットワーク

2611.03307.title: Safe-Ballbot: Tilt-Consistent MPC with Control Barrier Functions for Ballbot Navigation
2611.03307.abstract: Ball-balancing robots (ballbots) must lean to accelerate, and the lean is limited by the wheel torques and by safety. Planners that use the full robot model are expensive, while planners that ignore the balance dynamics produce references that cannot be followed. This paper presents a two-layer navigation scheme for a three-omni-wheel ballbot. The upper layer is a model predictive controller on a \emph{jerk model} of the ball position, with discrete-time control barrier functions for static, moving, rotating and concave obstacles. The lower layer is a hierarchical sliding mode controller with an extended state observer and a robust exponential control barrier function on the tilt (HSMC-ESO-ECBF). The layers are linked by an acceleration bound derived in closed form from the largest steady tilt that the barrier function admits, so that the plan never asks for a lean the tracker refuses. For obstacles whose motion is only predicted, the obstacles are inflated by conformal prediction radii that bound the prediction error with a prescribed probability. In MuJoCo, with omni-wheel roller contacts and torque saturation, the scheme keeps at least $10$\,cm of clearance, tracks the plan within $2$\,cm RMS, keeps the tilt below the limit and plans in $9$--$12$\,ms, $10$--$15$ times faster than a full-model nonlinear MPC that enters the inflated obstacles; with predicted obstacles, the conformal inflation removes the collisions of a constant-velocity predictor in $30$ random crossing scenarios and reduces them in an endless run on a closed path.The source code and video illustrations are available at https://safe-ballbot.github.io

llm.title_ja: Safe-Ballbot：ボールボットナビゲーションのための制御バリア関数を用いた傾き整合型MPC
llm.tldr_ja: 3オムニホイールのボールボットを対象に、ジャークモデルに基づく上位MPCと、傾きに対する堅牢な指数関数的制御バリア関数を持つ下位スライディングモードコントローラを組み合わせた二層ナビゲーションスキームを提案し、制約を守りつつ高速なプランニングを実現した。
llm.problem: 完全なモデルを使ったプランナーは計算コストが高く、バランス動力学を無視したプランナーは追従不可能な参照軌道を生成してしまう。
llm.method: ジャークモデルに基づく上位MPCと、傾きに対する制御バリア関数を持つ下位階層型スライディングモードコントローラを加速度境界で結合した二層ナビゲーションスキーム。
llm.result: MuJoCoのシミュレーションにおいて、完全モデルの非線形MPCの10〜15倍高速な9〜12msでプランニングを行い、障害物を回避しつつ目標に追従した。
keywords_ja: 実機シミュレーション

2611.03294.title: ForceLDM: A Force-aware Latent Dynamics Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
2611.03294.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires fine-grained control and complex physical interactions with the environment, posing significant challenges for robot policy learning. Vision-only policies struggle with such tasks, as contact states and interaction forces are difficult to infer from visual observations alone. Existing methods mitigate this issue by incorporating force or tactile sensing. However, they often treat these signals as auxiliary observations without fully exploiting their role in modeling future interaction dynamics. To address this, we propose ForceLDM, a force-aware latent dynamics model that learns future contact and motion dynamics to guide action generation. Rather than directly predicting future observations, which can entangle task-relevant dynamics with irrelevant sensory details, ForceLDM learns a compact representation of future dynamics through knowledge distillation. Specifically, a teacher network with privileged future force/torque and optical flow signals extracts future dynamic features, which are then distilled into a student network trained only on current observations. This enables the student model to reason about upcoming contacts and physical dynamics without relying on future sensory inputs at deployment. To improve robustness and generalization, we further introduce a curriculum-based progressive noise injection strategy to mitigate over-reliance on future features. Experiments on five real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks demonstrate that ForceLDM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, generalizes effectively to novel objects, and remains robust to environmental perturbations. Project page and code are available at https://tpy001.github.io/ForceLDM/.

llm.title_ja: ForceLDM：接触を伴うマニピュレーションのための力認識型潜在ダイナミクスモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の接触と運動のダイナミクスを教師なしで蒸留して学習する力認識型潜在ダイナミクスモデルForceLDMを提案し、接触の多いマニピュレーションタスクにおいて優れた一般化性能と頑健性を実証した。
llm.problem: 視覚のみのポリシーでは接触状態や相互作用の力を推論しにくく、接触の多いマニピュレーションの学習が困難である。
llm.method: 将来の力・トルクとオプティカルフローを用いた教師ネットワークから、現在観測のみの生徒ネットワークへ動的特徴を蒸留するForceLDMの提案。
llm.result: 5つの実世界の接触を伴うマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、既存の最先端ベースラインを上回り、未知のオブジェクトへも効果的に一般化した。
keywords_ja: 接触マニピュレーション
潜在ダイナミクスモデル

2611.03268.title: VerifLM: Physically Verified Image-Edit-Guided Goal Pose Generation for Robotic Manipulation
2611.03268.abstract: Many manipulation goals are easier to visualize than to specify numerically through explicit geometric constraints. We present VerifLM, a framework that converts image-edited goal configurations into physically verified 6-DoF object poses for planning. Using an edited image, VerifLM recovers an initial relative pose between an active object and a passive object, then prompts a vision-language model to generate axis-wise sampling constraints and a task-specific validation program. Candidate poses are evaluated in a physics simulator, and the VLM selects the most task-consistent retained candidate. To operate without predefined object meshes or physical parameters, VerifLM reconstructs metric object geometry from RGB-D observations and constructs multiple hypothetical simulations with varying physics and geometry. Parallel-world validation evaluates candidates across geometry--physics variations and ranks them by the number of worlds in which they satisfy the validation program. We evaluate VerifLM on nine manipulation tasks. VerifLM achieves the highest task success on eight of nine tasks, with the largest performance gain on goals requiring precise orientation and contact relationships.

llm.title_ja: VerifLM：ロボットマニピュレーションのための物理検証済み画像編集誘導型目標姿勢生成
llm.tldr_ja: 画像編集された目標構成から物理的に検証された6DoFの物体姿勢を生成するフレームワークVerifLMを提案し、9つのマニピュレーションタスクのうち8つで最高の成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: マニピュレーションの目標を数値的・幾何学的制約として明示的に指定することが難しい。
llm.method: 編集された画像から相対姿勢を復元し、VLMを用いてサンプリング制約と検証プログラムを生成、物理シミュレータと並列ワールド検証で候補姿勢を評価・選択する。
llm.result: 9つのマニピュレーションタスク中8つで最高のタスク成功率を達成し、特に正確な向きや接触関係を必要とする目標で大きな性能向上を示した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.03254.title: TRAILS: Trajectory Generation for Automated Indoor Locomotion Studies
2611.03254.abstract: Virtual reality experiments involving navigation and simulated robot motion often require large, realistic environments and numerous distinct trajectories to avoid repetitive navigation while providing sufficient variation for controlled experiments. Designing such scenarios manually is labor-intensive, particularly when trajectories must satisfy predefined geometric and kinematic constraints while remaining diverse and comparable across experimental conditions. This paper presents TRAILS, an automated framework for generating complete virtual navigation scenarios consisting of an environment layout, a path, and a time-parameterized motion profile. The framework combines a constraint-based procedural environment generator inspired by Wave Function Collapse, trajectory generation using optimized cubic Bézier curves, and speed-profile generation subject to kinematic constraints. The generated scenarios provide diverse indoor environments with corridors, open spaces, and obstacles, together with trajectories of identical duration that vary in path geometry, wall proximity, and velocity profiles while minimizing systematic dependencies between these characteristics. The framework is designed as an easy-to-use tool requiring only a small number of intuitive user-defined parameters to automatically generate large sets of distinct navigation scenarios satisfying prescribed geometric and kinematic constraints. By relying on explicit, seed-controlled algorithmic procedures rather than data-driven models, the generated scenarios remain transparent, reproducible, and configurable, making the framework well suited for telepresence and human-subject experiments. The code is available at https://github.com/JucciK/Trails .

llm.title_ja: TRAILS：自動屋内移動研究のための軌道生成
llm.tldr_ja: 制約ベースの手続型環境生成、3次ベジェ曲線を用いた軌道生成、速度プロファイル生成を組み合わせ、多様な屋内移動シナリオを自動生成するフレームワークTRAILSを提案した。
llm.problem: 制御された実験のための多様な屋内ナビゲーションシナリオを手動で設計することは労力がかかる。
llm.method: 波動関数崩壊法に着想を得た環境ジェネレータ、最適化されたベジェ曲線、運動学的制約に基づく速度プロファイル生成を組み合わせた自動フレームワーク。
llm.result: 幾何学的・運動学的制約を満たす、多様で再現性のある大規模な屋内ナビゲーションシナリオの自動生成を実現した。

2611.03216.title: Towards end-to-end co-design for one-shot printable task-specific soft robots
2611.03216.abstract: Soft robot co-design methods can jointly optimise morphology and control, but the resulting designs are often difficult to manufacture, while manufacturable approaches typically restrict actuator placement or require manual assembly. We present a simulation-based co-design framework that jointly optimises material distribution, pneumatic actuator placement and orientation, and control, while producing designs that can be fabricated monolithically using fused deposition modelling. The framework uses a differentiable 2D plane-stress Material Point Method simulator, incorporating an experimentally validated material model and an empirically derived surrogate model of a 3D-printed inflatable actuator. We demonstrate gradient-based optimisation soft robotic arms for prescribed tip trajectories. Optimised designs are transferred directly from simulation to one-shot monolithic FDM fabrication, with integrated actuators and no post-assembly. Physical experiments demonstrate that the resulting arms reproduce the behaviour predicted in simulation. This framework provides a path from task-level objectives to physically realisable soft robots while retaining substantial freedom over both morphology and actuation.

llm.title_ja: ワンショット印刷可能なタスク特化型ソフトロボットに向けたエンドツーエンドの共同設計
llm.tldr_ja: 材料分布、空気圧アクチュエータの配置・方向、制御を共同で最適化し、一体型で3Dプリント可能なソフトロボットのシミュレーションベースの共同設計フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: ソフトロボットの共同設計手法では形態と制御を最適化できても、製造が困難であるか、アクチュエータ配置が制限される。
llm.method: 実験的に検証された材料モデルとサーロゲートモデルを組み込んだ、微分可能な2D平面応力材料点法シミュレータを用いた勾配ベースの最適化フレームワーク。
llm.result: 最適化された設計をシミュレーションからFDM方式によるワンショット一体成形へ直接転写し、物理実験においてシミュレーション通りの挙動を再現した。

2611.03189.title: MoSoLoco: Monocular 3D Human Localization through Visual Latent Features and Social Context
2611.03189.abstract: Estimating the metric 3D position of people from a monocular camera is important for robot navigation and motion prediction. Lightweight pose-based localizers are attractive for robotic hardware with limited computational resources because they operate on compact 2D keypoints. However, they typically discard the richer visual representations computed by the pose estimator. We introduce MoSoLoco, a per-frame monocular 3D human localizer that combines the pose detector's internal visual features with the detected 2D skeleton, without requiring an additional RGB or depth encoder. MoSoLoco can further incorporate sparse same-frame multi-person context to refine individual position estimates. Experiments on JRDB and NuScenes show that reusing pose-detector representations improves localization, reducing the best JRDB error by approximately 23 percent relative to the strongest evaluated keypoint-based baseline. A sparse social-interaction module incorporates nearby detections from the same image for further refinement. Controlled trajectory-forecasting experiments show downstream benefits, while the complete pipeline remains suitable for efficient Jetson AGX Xavier inference.

llm.title_ja: MoSoLoco：視覚的潜在特徴と社会的文脈を通じた単眼3D人間ローカライゼーション
llm.tldr_ja: ポーズ推定器の内部視覚特徴と検出された2D骨格を組み合わせ、スパースなマルチ人の文脈を統合することで、効率的な単眼3D人間位置推定を実現するMoSoLocoを提案した。
llm.problem: 軽量なポーズベースのローカライザーはコンパクトな2Dキーポイントで動作するが、ポーズ推定器が計算した豊かな視覚表現を破棄してしまっている。
llm.method: 追加のRGB/深度エンコーダーなしで、ポーズ検出器の内部視覚特徴と2Dスケルトンを結合し、スパースな社会的相互作用モジュールで位置推定を洗練させるフレームワーク。
llm.result: JRDBやNuScenesの実験において、ポーズ検出器の表現の再利用によりローカライゼーション精度が向上し、JRDBの最強のベースラインと比較して誤差を約23%削減した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2611.03168.title: Rollout then Recycle: 3,718 Labelled Real-Robot Episodes from Benchmarking 7 Policies on 12 Tasks
2611.03168.abstract: We release all 3,718 episodes from the ArmnetBench v0.1 evaluation (arXiv:2607.24481), which contains 600 teleoperated demonstrations and 3,118 rollouts of seven imitation-learning and vision-language-action policies on 12 tabletop tasks, recorded on low-cost SO-101 arms; 73% of the rollouts are failures. Every policy for a task was trained or fine-tuned on the same 50 demonstrations and rolled out on the same cell, so the corpus contains many policies' failures on shared tasks. An operator labelled every rollout successful, suboptimal or failure. Each episode has three camera views, joint states and actions and is available on the Hugging Face Hub in LeRobot v3.0 and a reward-model format. This note documents how the episodes were collected and the limitations that could affect their use.
2611.03168.comment: 4 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Accepted to the "Oops, I Erred" Workshop at CoRL 2026

llm.title_ja: ロールアウトして再利用：12のタスクにおける7つのポリシーのベンチマークから得られた3,718件のラベル付き実機ロボットエピソード
llm.tldr_ja: 低コストなSO-101アームを用いて12の卓上タスクで収集した、7つの模倣学習・VLAポリシーによる3,718件のロールアウトおよび実演データセットを公開した。
llm.problem: ロボット学習において、失敗例を含む多様で大規模な実機評価データセットが不足している。
llm.method: 低コストなSO-101アームを用いて、同一のタスクとデモンストレーションで複数の模倣学習・VLAポリシーを実行し、すべてのロールアウトを成功・最適未満・失敗に手動で分類する。
llm.result: 3つのカメラ視点、関節状態、行動を含む3,718件のエピソードデータセットをHugging Face Hubに公開し、その収集方法と限界を文書化した。

2611.03163.title: FineCraft: Enhancing VLA Models for Fine-Grained Manipulation
2611.03163.abstract: Fine-grained manipulation couples instruction grounding, local visual precision, and sustained execution. We present FineCraft, a framework that adapts pretrained models for fine-grained manipulation in the MetaFine Challenge. A task-routed mixture of policies selects independently adapted DINOv2-DiT or pretrained $π_{0.5}$ policies through a common observation-action interface. Local visual features help identify the instructed object parts, demonstrations and expert continuations teach the required actions, and new observations guide replanning during execution. FineCraft ranks fourth with an overall score of $0.878$, exceeding the published reference on all five tasks. Official results and local diagnostics characterize performance across visual perturbations, instruction changes, and multi-stage manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/eqcy/FineCraft

llm.title_ja: FineCraft：きめ細かなマニピュレーションに向けたVLAモデルの拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みモデルを適応させ、タスクに応じたポリシーの混合を用いてきめ細かなマニピュレーションを実現するフレームワークFineCraftを提案し、MetaFineチャレンジで4位を獲得した。
llm.problem: きめ細かなマニピュレーションでは、指示の接地、局所的な視覚的精度、および持続的な実行の結合が求められるが困難である。
llm.method: 共通の観測-行動インターフェースを介して、独立に適応させたDINOv2-DiTまたはπ0.5ポリシーを選択するタスクルーティングされたポリシー混合フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: MetaFineチャレンジの5つのすべてのタスクで公開リファレンスを上回り、全体スコア0.878で4位を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.03138.title: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL
2611.03138.abstract: Progress in robot learning, particularly physical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is currently challenged by a limited availability of accessible, standardized benchmarks. While simulation-based MARL has produced remarkable emergent behaviors, from coordinated team play to complex tool use, translating these advances to physical systems remains difficult. A key barrier is infrastructural: physical platforms are often prohibitively expensive, require specialized facilities, or lack open mechanisms and designs for reproducibility. We introduce KlaskTron, an open-source, low-cost (<\$2500 USD), desktop-scale robotic testbed for adversarial MARL based on the dynamic tabletop game KLASK. The platform features dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors, enabling the high-speed, precise manipulation required for competitive play. Crucially, we provide a complete ecosystem: hardware designs (CAD, BOM), a GPU-native digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Lab for high-fidelity modeling and simulation, and a validated sim-to-real baseline using a learned neural actuator model. We demonstrate that this baseline enables zero-shot policy transfer, with trained agents exhibiting emergent adversarial behaviors. To ensure full reproducibility of our results, all project assets are released publicly: hardware CAD/BOM and assembly documentation at [https://idscethzurich.github.io/klask_hardware], inference software stack at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_software] and the simulation and MARL setup at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_rl].
2611.03138.journal_ref: Proceedings of Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS), Sydney, Australia, July 2026

llm.title_ja: KlaskTron：物理的敵対的マルチエージェント強化学習のためのオープンソースプラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 卓上ゲームKLASKをベースにした低コストなオープンソースのデスクトップ型ロボットテストベッドKlaskTronを開発し、ゼロショットでの実機転移を実証した。
llm.problem: 物理的なマルチエージェント強化学習（MARL）の進展は、アクセスしやすく標準化されたアクセシブルなベンチマークの不足によって妨げられている。
llm.method: 高トルクブラシレスモーターを備えたデュアルCoreXYガントリー、NVIDIA Isaac LabでのGPUネイティブデジタルツイン、学習済みニューラルアクチュエータモデルを用いたSim-to-Realベースラインの開発。
llm.result: 学習済みエージェントが新たな敵対的行動を示すとともに、ゼロショットでのポリシーの実機転移に成功した。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント強化学習
ロボットテストベッド

2611.03125.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
2611.03125.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.
2611.03125.comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, Accepted by Medical Image Analysis

llm.title_ja: SurgPace：外科用マルチモーダル大規模言語モデルのための複雑度を考慮したプログレッシブ蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: 予測信頼性と幾何学的一貫性からサンプルの複雑度を推定し、段階的なカリキュラム学習によってコンパクトでメモリ効率の高い外科用マルチモーダル大規模言語モデルを構築するSurgPaceを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）の計算コストが高いため臨床展開が制限されるが、外科データは難易度や文脈が大きく異なるため一様な教師・生徒間転移が不安定になる。
llm.method: 予測信頼性とローレンツ幾何学的一貫性を用いてサンプル複雑度を推定し、階層的な表現アライメントと組み合わせた継続的カリキュラムフレームワークSurgPaceの提案。
llm.result: 外科用データセットのベンチマークにおいて、既存のMLLM蒸留ベースラインを常に上回り、高速なデコードとメモリ効率の向上を実証した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2611.03106.title: A Tightly Coupled Magnetic-Inertial SLAM System for Field Robots
2611.03106.abstract: Field robots operating in mines, tunnels, and disaster areas require reliable localization despite GNSS denial and degraded camera and LiDAR measurements caused by dust, smoke, or poor illumination. Missions involving both ground and aerial robots further motivate complementary sensing modalities that do not depend on visibility, preinstalled infrastructure, or wheel contact. This letter presents MISLAM, a tightly coupled magnetic-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping system using an IMU and a nine-magnetometer array, without relying on external odometry or platform-specific motion assumptions. The system combines the inertial navigation model with local polynomial magnetic-field models for short-term motion estimation and a global Gaussian process model for drift correction using an error-state Kalman filter. Offline evaluation on three indoor datasets collected with a handheld rig shows reductions in total endpoint closure error of 45.7% - 78.0% relative to magnetic-inertial odometry. Under poor illumination, MISLAM maintains tracking after visual-inertial odometry fails, achieving a horizontal closure error of 0.332 m, although vertical drift remains a limitation. These results support magnetic-inertial SLAM as a complementary localization modality for robotic sensor suites operating under degraded visual conditions.

llm.title_ja: フィールドロボットのための緊密結合型磁気-慣性SLAMシステム
llm.tldr_ja: IMUと磁力計アレイを組み合わせ、外部オドメトリに依存せずに短期的運動推定とドリフト補正を行う緊密結合型磁気-慣性SLAMシステムMISLAMを提案し、視覚情報の劣化した環境での位置推定性能を示した。
llm.problem: 鉱山、トンネル、災害現場などのフィールドロボットでは、GNSSが使えず、粉塵や煙、照明不良によりカメラやLiDARの計測が劣化する。
llm.method: 慣性航法モデルと局所多項式磁場モデルを組み合わせた短期運動推定と、大域的ガウス過程モデルによるドリフト補正をエラー状態カルマンフィルターで統合したMISLAMの提案。
llm.result: 視覚慣性オドメトリが追跡に失敗する劣悪な照明下でも追跡を維持し、ハンドヘルドデータセットにおいてエンドポイント誤差を大幅に削減した。
llm.limitation: 垂直方向のドリフトが依然として制限として残る。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.03103.title: VLALagBench: Understanding When and Why VLA Inference Latency Matters
2611.03103.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a promising path toward general-purpose robot manipulation. While inference latency can affect task success in a constantly evolving physical world, the relationship between latency and task success rate remains poorly understood. In this paper, we introduce VLALagBench, a comprehensive benchmark for studying VLA inference latency sensitivity across task types, object speeds, execution modes (synchronous and asynchronous), and VLA policies. Using VLALagBench, we find that even a modest inference latency of 100 ms can nearly halve task success on moving targets, with sensitivity varying substantially across tasks and policies. These differences reflect task-specific requirements for precision and continuous motion. By overlapping inference with action execution, asynchronous execution can recover some of the lost success at the cost of more frequent inference requests. Building on these findings, we develop an empirical model that predicts task success from limited calibration data, achieving root-mean-square prediction errors of only 5.7-7.8% across various VLA policies. Given an inference system's latency and per-robot throughput, these predictions guide the selection of system-specific VLA algorithm configurations to maximize task success. We believe VLALagBench and these findings provide a solid foundation for future robotics algorithm-system co-design.

llm.title_ja: VLALagBench：VLA推論遅延がいつ、なぜ重要になるかの理解
llm.tldr_ja: VLAモデルの推論遅延がタスク成功率に与える影響を体系的に評価するベンチマークVLALagBenchを開発し、100msの遅延でも動的ターゲットに対する成功率が半減することなどを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 物理世界において推論遅延がタスク成功に与える影響や、遅延と成功率の関係性が十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: タスクの種類、物体の速度、実行モード、VLAポリシーを網羅的に変化させて遅延感度を評価する総合的ベンチマークVLALagBenchの構築と、成功率を予測する empirical モデルの開発。
llm.result: わずか100msの遅延でも移動体に対する成功率が半減することを突き止め、較正データから成功率を5.7〜7.8%のRMSEで予測するモデルを構築した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル
ロボットマニピュレーション
アルゴリズムシステム共同設計

2611.03091.title: KlaskTron-IL: A Contact-Rich Adversarial Imitation Learning Benchmark with a Validated Sim-to-Real Bridge
2611.03091.abstract: KlaskTron is an open-hardware physical platform for two-player adversarial reinforcement learning, with a learned actuator model that supports zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of trained policies. Building on this platform, we contribute KlaskTron-IL: a multi-tier imitation learning dataset (80k human demonstration timesteps collected directly on the physical robot, 320k symmetry-augmented timesteps, and synthetic expert trajectories up to 5M steps generated by the zero-shot-validated PPO policy), and diagnostic baselines that expose three characteristic failure modes of standard IL methods under contact-rich adversarial dynamics: BC's data scaling plateau, GAIL's interpretable but weak-gradient discriminator (Spearman $ρ= -1.0$ peg-ball proximity recovery, but a logit span under 0.1), and an asymmetric BC-prior x reward-density interaction. Because the policy interface used throughout this paper is the same one the actuator model bridges to hardware, a policy trained on this benchmark can run unchanged on the physical robot, as we demonstrate zero-shot for the strongest BC baseline, so long as its commands respect the actuator model's $\pm 0.2$ m/s identification range.

llm.title_ja: KlaskTron-IL：検証済みシムツリアルブリッジを備えた接触を伴う敵対的模倣学習ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的プラットフォームKlaskTronを拡張し、実機デモや対称性拡張、合成専門家軌道を含むマルチティアな模倣学習データセットKlaskTron-ILを構築して、接触の多いダイナミクスにおける模倣学習手法の失敗モードを分析した。
llm.problem: 接触の多い敵対的ダイナミクスの下で、標準的な模倣学習手法が持つ固有の失敗モードや限界が十分に明らかにされていない。
llm.method: 物理ロボットで直接収集したデモ、対称性拡張データ、PPOポリシーによる合成軌道を含むマルチティアな模倣学習データセット（KlaskTron-IL）の構築と診断的ベースラインの評価。
llm.result: BCのデータスケーリングの頭打ちやGAILの弱い勾配識別器などの特徴的な失敗モードを暴露し、学習したポリシーをアクチュエータモデルを介して実機でゼロショット実行できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 接触マニピュレーション

2611.03067.title: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
2611.03067.abstract: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

llm.title_ja: PlanContext：文脈に応じた運転意思決定のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 観測されたシーンを固定したまま高レベルの運転意図を変化させるペア評価により、文脈に応じた意思決定を評価するベンチマークPlanContextを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のエンドツーエンド運転ベンチマークは軌道品質を主評価しており、文脈に依存した意思決定の特性評価が不十分である。
llm.method: シーン条件を固定して高レベル運転意図を変化させたペア評価を構築し、6つの代表的な運転文脈で文脈的決定の正しさ、道路順守、動的安全性を評価するフレームワーク。
llm.result: 23の公開エンドツーエンド運転モデルの実験により、従来の運転品質スコアの高さが必ずしも強力な文脈的意思決定力に直結しないことを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習

2611.03063.title: Networked AI: Architecture, Theory, and Applications
2611.03063.abstract: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly large-scale deep learning, have been driven by monolithic or offline training on massive curated datasets. While successful, these approaches face structural limitations: escalating data and computational demands, limited online adaptability, and a lack of system-level intelligence in open, non-stationary environments. This paper presents Networked AI - a networked intelligent system composed of interacting, heterogeneous, and continuously evolving AI agents. We establish a hierarchical layered architecture comprising an Agent Layer for heterogeneous capability construction, an Interaction Layer for signal-processing-guided online data extraction, and a Regulation Layer for stability-constrained collective evolution. Foundations in data science, signal processing, and system control are hereby synthesized into a unified theoretical framework of Networked AI, providing superior data efficiency, intelligence efficiency, interpretability, and scalability. Theoretical and experimental analysis demonstrates that Networked AI can approach near-linear scaling in resource demand, in contrast to the exponential increase in standalone end-to-end systems. It provides not only online adaptation to out-of-distribution environmental novelties, but also the autonomous evolution towards application-specific intelligence. Application frontiers are discussed for IoT spaces, embodied, spatial, and industrial intelligences, as well as the cellular infrastructure and beyond. Key open challenges are identified towards realizing locally autonomous, collectively intelligent, continuously evolving, globally regulated Networked AI.

llm.title_ja: ネットワーク化されたAI：アーキテクチャ、理論、および応用
llm.tldr_ja: 異種かつ進化するAIエージェントの相互作用に基づく階層的アーキテクチャ「Networked AI」を提案し、データ効率、解釈可能性、スケーラビリティの向上を理論および実験で示した。
llm.problem: 従来のモノリス型またはオフライン学習による大規模AIは、データ・計算需要の増大、オンライン適応性の限界、オープン環境でのシステム知能の欠如という構造的制限に直面している。
llm.method: エージェント層、インタラクション層、レギュレーション層からなる階層的レイヤーアーキテクチャの構築と、データ科学・信号処理・システム制御の統合による統一理論フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: 従来のエンドツーエンドシステムの指数関数的増大とは対照的に、リソース需要においてほぼ線形のスケーリングに近づき、分布外の新規環境へのオンライン適応を実現した。
keywords_ja: エージェントシステム

2611.03059.title: BeyondContact: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Airflow-Based Non-Contact Manipulation
2611.03059.abstract: Contact-based robotic manipulation is constrained by end-effector reachability and the mechanical properties of objects. Airflow can exert forces without direct robot-object contact, enabling manipulation of objects beyond the reach or when direct contact is undesirable. However, the lack of suitable simulation has hindered the application of reinforcement learning to airflow-based manipulation, limiting the broader adoption of this mechanism compared with contact-based methods. To address this gap, we developed a robot- and task-agnostic airflow extension for Isaac Lab that supports massively parallel training. The extension uses experimentally identified airflow models to compute the forces and torques exerted on objects. Based on this extension, we train a hybrid push-blow (HPB) policy that combines contact-based pushing with airflow manipulation and a rectangular reorientation (RR) policy that controls a cuboid's heading using airflow alone. To enable physical execution, we design a lightweight, high-speed blower that coexists with a gripper. In zero-shot real-world deployment, HPB achieves an 80% success rate over 20 trials, while RR achieves a mean absolute heading error of 2.6 degrees across four target headings. The project materials are available at https://github.com/iit-DLSLab/BeyondContact.
2611.03059.comment: Peiyu Yang and Mohamad S. Moudallal contributed equally. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

llm.title_ja: BeyondContact：気流ベースの非接触マニピュレーションのための強化学習フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: Isaac Lab向けにロボット非依存の気流拡張機能を開発し、接触ベースの押しと気流操作を組み合わせたハイブリッドポリシー等の訓練と実機でのゼロショット展開に成功した。
llm.problem: 接触型ロボットマニピュレーションはエンドエフェクタのリーチや物体の機械的特性に制約され、気流を利用した非接触操作に対する適切なシミュレーションが不足していた。
llm.method: 実験的に特定された気流モデルを使用して物体に加わる力を計算する、Isaac Lab向けのロボットおよびタスク非依存の気流拡張機能と、それを用いた強化学習ポリシーの訓練。
llm.result: 実機におけるゼロショット展開において、ハイブリッドプッシュ・ブローポリシーが20試行で80%の成功率を達成し、長距離・非接触操作の有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: 非接触マニピュレーション

2611.03016.title: Swarm Choreography Made Simple: Superposed Guiding Vector Fields for Rigid Formation Path Following
2611.03016.abstract: This paper presents a decentralized guiding vector field framework for rigid formation path following in multi- UAV systems based on the superposition of simple rule-driven vector fields. Each control objective is encoded as a dedicated vector-field component: a normalized tangential term to ensure progression along a prescribed geometric path at a desired speed, a convergence term driving the formation toward the path, a local coordination term that preserves the desired formation shape through a pseudo-path parameter, and a local separation term for inter-agent collision avoidance. The coordination mechanism requires the exchange of only a single scalar per agent, resulting in low communication bandwidth. Partial theoretical results establish convergence of the swarm to the desired path and formation in the absence of the sepa- ration term, while collision avoidance is formally guaranteed. The approach is experimentally validated using a swarm of five quadrotors executing two 3D choreographies. The first experiment involves tracking a helical path while maintaining a rigid V-shaped formation. The second demonstrates a spiral- like motion obtained by a rotating circular formation tracking a vertical line. The experimental results support the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed framework.
2611.03016.journal_ref: ICUAS - International Conference on Unmanned Aircraft Systems, Jun 2026, Corfu, Greece

llm.title_ja: 簡単に実現する群ロボットの振付：剛体隊列の経路追従のための重ね合わせ誘導ベクトル場
llm.tldr_ja: 単純なルール駆動型ベクトル場の重ね合わせに基づく、マルチUAVシステムのための分散型誘導ベクトル場フレームワークを提案し、5機のクアッドロコプターによる3D空間での実証に成功した。
llm.problem: マルチUAVシステムにおいて、剛体隊列を維持しながら障害物を回避しつつ所定の経路に追従するための低帯域かつ分散型の制御が求められる。
llm.method: 接線項、収束項、局所調整項、局所分離項を専用のベクトル場コンポーネントとして符号化し、エージェント間でスカラー1つを交換するだけで剛体隊列と衝突回避を両立する分散型フレームワーク。
llm.result: 5機のクアッドロコプターを用いたV字型隊列のヘリカル経路追従や、回転する円形隊列による垂直線追従などの3D振付実験により有効性を実証した。
llm.limitation: 分離項を除いた場合には、隊列と経路への収束は部分的な理論結果のみである。

2611.03015.title: Comparative study of global pooling for pre-departure ship fuel consumption prediction: Advantages over per-ship and adaptation-based approaches
2611.03015.abstract: Most fuel oil consumption (FOC) models for voyage planning are per-ship models and thus generalize poorly beyond each vessel's records. Transfer and federated learning have been reported to perform better, but under different protocols that often use inputs unavailable before departure or random data splits. It therefore remains unclear which approach performs best. In this study, we compare 11 per-ship, adaptation-based, and global methods on 21 vessels. To prevent leakage, all methods receive identical inputs known or forecast before departure, excluding engine RPM and shaft power, and are tested on intact voyage legs after all training records of each vessel. Global pooling, in which one model describes each vessel by its ship identity and seven ship specifications, performs best overall in every setting examined. For in-fleet vessels, Global LightGBM reaches an overall MAPE of 8.92%, against 11.14% for Per-Ship LightGBM, and outperforms every per-ship and adaptation-based model. Global models of five architectures, including a Transformer, all outperform the per-ship and federated models. Fine-tuning a global model for each vessel, even by low-rank adaptation of the Transformer, adds no accuracy. Without any records of a vessel, the global model reaches a median MAPE of 11.20% and outperforms a per-ship model trained on that vessel's records for 14 of 21 vessels. Adding its first records to the pooled data is as accurate as vessel-specific adaptation. Ship identity and specifications are largely interchangeable for in-fleet vessels, but only the specifications support zero-shot prediction. Its error grows as a vessel's specifications differ from the fleet's. Per-ship models and vessel-specific adaptation are therefore unnecessary under fair comparison. One global model can serve a whole fleet, including newly delivered vessels with similar specifications.

llm.title_ja: 出港前船舶燃料消費量予測における大域的プーリングの比較研究：個別船舶および適応型アプローチに対する優位性
llm.tldr_ja: 出港前に利用可能なデータのみを用いて、21隻の船舶データを対象に11種類の燃料消費予測モデルを比較し、船舶識別情報と仕様を用いた大域的プーリング手法が最も優れた性能を発揮することを示した。
llm.problem: 航海計画のための燃料油消費量モデルは個別船舶モデルが主流であるが一般化性能が低く、転移学習や連合学習との比較における公平な検証が不足していた。
llm.method: エンジンRPMや軸馬力などの出港前に入手できない入力を除外し、同一の入力条件のもとで11の個別・適応・大域的手法を21隻のデータで厳密に比較評価する。
llm.result: 船舶IDと7つの仕様記述を用いた大域的プーリング（例：Global LightGBM）が全設定において最良の精度（MAPE 8.92%）を達成し、個別モデルや適応モデルが不要であることを示した。

2611.02999.title: SyncHeC: Markerless Spatio-Temporal Hand-Eye Calibration via Differentiable Rendering and Continuous-Time Joint Optimization
2611.02999.abstract: Markerless hand-eye calibration under continuous motion requires jointly resolving camera geometry and the time offset between images and joint states. We present SyncHeC (Synchronized Hand-Eye Calibration), a dense differentiable-rendering framework that estimates both from a single robot trajectory. Continuous-time forward kinematics makes latency differentiable, metric depth complements mask contours, and an offline planner combines spatial sensitivity with temporal excitation. Alternating updates support Eye-to-Hand, Eye-in-Hand, and multi-camera calibration. On a 7-DoF arm, one $6.5$\,s motion yields $0.21$\,cm translation error against a marker-board reference, $0.34$\,cm touch-test error, and $2.7$\,ms latency error relative to an $87$\,ms reference with $95\%$ uncertainty of $\pm1.5$\,ms. Against CM-Calib on matched recordings, translation and nominal latency errors improve by $3.7\times$ and $2.3\times$. Experiments span seven arms and four depth sensors. Compensating the recovered offset during policy training and deployment increases success by $8.1$ percentage points across six families and six tasks ($1{,}800$ matched pairs; paired $95\%$ confidence interval $[6.3,9.9]$ points).

llm.title_ja: SyncHeC：微分可能レンダリングと連続時間共同最適化によるマーカーレス時空間手眼キャリブレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 連続的な動きからカメラ幾何学と時間オフセットを同時に解く、高密度な微分可能レンダリングを用いたマーカーレス手眼キャリブレーションフレームワークSyncHeCを提案し、従来法を大きく上回る精度とタスク成功率の向上を達成した。
llm.problem: 連続運動下でのマーカーレス手眼キャリブレーションでは、カメラ幾何学と画像・関節状態間の時間オフセットを同時に解決する必要があるが困難である。
llm.method: 連続時間の順運動学により遅延を微分可能にし、深度情報をマスク輪郭に補完、オフラインプランナーを組み合わせた高密度微分可能レンダリングフレームワークSyncHeCの提案。
llm.result: 7軸アームでの実験において、マーカーボード基準に対して翻訳誤差0.21cm、遅延誤差2.7msを達成し、ポリシーの訓練と展開時に適用することで6つのタスクで成功率を8.1ポイント向上させた。
keywords_ja: 手眼キャリブレーション
微分可能レンダリング
センサーフュージョン

2611.02992.title: MS-DOTT: A Multi-Modal Dataset for Off-Road Traversability Estimation
2611.02992.abstract: Autonomous robots are gaining traction in off-road environments, driven by their rising demand in agriculture, defense, and search-and-rescue operations. However, these environments are inherently unpredictable and navigation remains a formidable challenge given the complex environmental conditions including challenging terrain and varying illumination. Off-road autonomy requires robust perception across multiple spatial scales and imaging modalities, yet most sensing setups struggle to capture both far-field environmental context and near-field terrain detail simultaneously across various illumination conditions. To facilitate development of robust off-road perception and traversability estimation systems, we propose MS-DOTT (Multi-Sensor Dataset for Off-road Terrain Traversability) a comprehensive multi-modal off-road dataset with long-range 3D sensing and short-range, fine-grained perception to facilitate high-fidelity terrain understanding by combining proprioceptive signals for tracking vehicle dynamics with exteroceptive imaging and pointcloud data. The dataset includes trajectories recorded across nominal lighting, low-light, and no-light conditions with diverse 2D and 3D sensing for both long-range large-scale and short-range high-resolution sensing, as well as 4D RADAR measurements that provide velocity estimates for detected pointclouds. We demonstrate the utility of the dataset by adapting a SOTA multi-sensor fusion method for the purpose of traversability estimation. This dataset will aid the robotics community in advancing research and development of methods for traversability estimation, off-road perception and multi-sensor fusion in unstructured environments.

llm.title_ja: MS-DOTT：オフロード走行可能性推定のためのマルチモーダルデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: オフロード環境での頑健な知覚と走行可能性推定システムの開発を促進するため、長距離3Dセンシングと短距離の微細な知覚を組み合わせた包括的なマルチモーダルデータセットであるMS-DOTTを提案する。
llm.problem: オフロード環境は予測不能であり、複雑な地形や照明条件の変化の下でのナビゲーションは困難である。
llm.method: 車両ダイナミクスを追跡する固有受容信号と、外受容イメージングおよびポイントクラウドデータを組み合わせた長・短距離のマルチセンサーデータセットを構築した。
llm.result: SOTAのマルチセンサーフュージョン手法を走行可能性推定に適応させることで、データセットの有用性を実証した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.02968.title: ReContact: Reconstruct and Retarget Human Contacts from Video for Contact-Rich Humanoid Manipulation
2611.02968.abstract: Contact transitions allow humanoid robots to redistribute object support across the whole body, enabling manipulation beyond hand-only grasps. Human videos provide a scalable source of such transitions for robots to learn from. However, body occlusion disrupts object pose tracking and corrupts retargeted motion. Moreover, accurately reproducing the object trajectory does not ensure that the robot applies stabilizing forces at the intended contacts, risking slips or drops in later phases. To address these challenges, we propose ReContact, which reconstructs and retargets human-object interactions through an object-centric contact plan. The plan specifies contact phases, contact pairs, anchors, pressing directions, and sticking or sliding modes. Contact priors stabilize object pose reconstruction through occlusion.
