keywords_ja: インタラクティブ運転

2611.02236.title: Iterative Gumbel Planning for Continuous Control
2611.02236.abstract: Search-based planning remains a powerful policy improvement paradigm in reinforcement learning, driving milestone successes in discrete domains. However, extending this paradigm to continuous control exposes a structural mismatch: search evaluates a finite set of action candidates, whereas continuous RL typically relies on Gaussian policies. We show that winner-action distillation into a continuous Gaussian induces a \textit{projection error} and a stepwise variance-expanding gradient tendency when the selected action is sufficiently far from the current mean. Empirically, this tendency is associated with elevated terminal variance and a return gap on the evaluated tasks. To address this, we propose \textbf{Iterative Gumbel Planning (IGP)}. By adopting a per-dimension factorized categorical policy, IGP naturally aligns the policy support with the search candidates, eliminating the projection error and reducing the residual approximation to a bounded discretization error. To bypass the combinatorial explosion of high-dimensional discrete action spaces, IGP pairs Gumbel Top-$K$ candidate sampling with an MPPI-style multi-round iterative search to refine the policy at each state. Empirically, IGP achieves state-of-the-art aggregate performance and sample efficiency on DMControl and HumanoidBench. Furthermore, it produces more stable action sequences with lower temporal variance, demonstrating its practical potential for real-world robotic deployment.

llm.title_ja: 連続制御のための反復ガンベル計画法
llm.tldr_ja: 連続制御への探索ベース計画の適用における射影誤差を解消するため、次元ごとの因子分解カテゴリカルポリシーとGumbel Top-Kサンプリングを組み合わせた「反復ガンベル計画（IGP）」を提案した。
llm.problem: 探索が有限の候補集合を評価するのに対し連続RLはガウス方針に依存するため、連続制御への拡張において構造的なミスマッチが生じる点。
llm.method: 次元ごとに因子分解されたカテゴリカルポリシーを採用し、Gumbel Top-K候補サンプリングとMPPIスタイルの複数回反復探索を組み合わせて各状態で方針を洗練させる。
llm.result: DMControlおよびHumanoidBenchにおいて、最先端の総合性能とサンプル効率を達成し、時間的分散の低い安定した行動シーケンスを生成した。

2611.02218.title: Beyond Ensemble Disagreement: Predictive STL Monitoring of RL Locomotion under Distribution Shift
2611.02218.abstract: RL locomotion policies trained under nominal simulation conditions may encounter distribution shifts that compromise safety. Predictive monitors could anticipate violations, but their world-model forecasts may become unreliable under shift, and ensemble disagreement is not calibrated. We evaluate predictive Signal Temporal Logic (STL) monitoring for frozen Ant-v5 and HalfCheetah-v5 policies using closed-loop world-model rollouts and a three-model ensemble. Across external-force, observation-noise, and mass shifts, predicted robustness ranks HalfCheetah's future STL violations strongly, whereas disagreement does not reliably track observation prediction error or violations. Under severe noise, violations remain common ($64.2\pm24.4\%$ at $K{=}20$ across three PPO seeds), yet current-state robustness without prediction comes within $0.03$ AUROC of predictive robustness. Penalizing predicted robustness by disagreement does not consistently improve ranking. Ant provides complementary per-specification evidence, but its composite target has no positive violations and its any-violation target is single-class in most evaluated seed-condition slices. Overall, predictive robustness provides useful STL-specific ranking but little demonstrated additional ranking value over the current state; these findings caution against treating ensemble disagreement as a reliable indicator of safety uncertainty.
2611.02218.comment: Accepted at the Modeling Uncertainty in Robotic World Models Workshop CoRL 2026

llm.title_ja: アンサンブルの不一致を超えて：分布シフト下における強化学習移動制御の予測的STLモニタリング
llm.tldr_ja: 閉ループワールドモデルロールアウトと3モデルのアンサンブルを用いて、凍結されたAnt-v5およびHalfCheetah-v5ポリシーに対する予測的シグナル時相論理（STL）モニタリングを評価した。
llm.problem: 名目上のシミュレーション条件で訓練された強化学習移動ポリシーが、安全性を損なう分布シフトに直面する可能性がある点。
llm.method: 閉ループワールドモデルロールアウトと3モデルアンサンブルを活用した予測的STLモニタリングにより、将来のSTL違反を評価する。
llm.result: 予測的頑健性はHalfCheetahの将来のSTL違反を強力にランク付けする一方で、不一致は観測予測誤差や違反を信頼性高く追跡しないことを示した。

2611.02189.title: Directional Bounded-Confidence Matrix Alignment in Vicsek Flocking
2611.02189.abstract: This paper proposes a directional bounded-confidence variant of the discrete-time Vicsek multiagent model, in which pairwise heading alignment is modulated by a state-dependent, positive semidefinite matrix that independently gates orthogonal radial and tangential components in the instantaneous line-of-sight frame. We analyze the normalized, matrix-weighted system dynamics, proving a uniform non-vanishing bound on proposal vectors that guarantees global well-posedness across arbitrary network states. For local small-spread states under complete metric interaction, we prove linear geometric contraction of the heading diameter and establish an offline-verifiable spatial bootstrap condition that guarantees metric contact preservation and coincidence avoidance a priori. A counterexample demonstrates invariant polarized states on connected matrix graphs, delineating systemic structural limits. Numerical experiments against unfiltered Vicsek averaging, scalar tied confidence, trace-matched scalar baselines, and restricted-angle rules demonstrate component-selective filtering without rejected-channel leakage, along with improved fixed-bound alignment on multi-seed benchmarks across varying population densities.

llm.title_ja: Vicsek群れモデルにおける方向性付き有界信頼行列整列
llm.tldr_ja: ペアの進行方向整列を状態依存の半正定値行列で変調する離散時間Vicsekマルチエージェントモデルの方向性付き有界信頼バリアントを提案し、大域的な整列挙動と数学的保証を解析した。
llm.problem: 従来のVicsekモデルにおけるフィルタリングや整列の限界や、直交する半径方向・接線方向の成分を独立に制御する枠組みの欠如。
llm.method: 瞬時の視線フレーム内で直交する半径方向および接線方向の成分を独立にゲートする、状態依存の半正定値行列を用いたモデルの動特性を解析・証明する。
llm.result: 任意のネットワーク状態にわたる大域的な適切性を保証する一様な非ゼロのバウンドを証明し、数値実験によりチャネル漏れのない成分選択的フィルタリングを確認した。
keywords_ja: 行列重み付きダイナミクス

2611.02181.title: Human Sensorimotor Model Adaptation to Account for Robot Accuracy and Speed Augmentation in Human-Robot Co-Manipulation
2611.02181.abstract: In human-robot co-manipulation, the robot's trajectory should accommodate the human's, where human sensorimotor behavior is affected by the task's spatial and temporal constraints, as well as personal factors. Several robot trajectory planning methods have been proposed to embed human sensorimotor models in the robot trajectory planning, but these methods do not consider temporal constraints that adapt to how the human behaves when interacting with the robot. To better align human and robot collaborative motion, this work adapts a stochastic optimal control problem with a final state constraint from the task constraints and a temporal constraint from Fitts' law. A recursive least squares method is used to estimate the Fitts' law parameters, adapting the robot's motion duration to that of the human, thus allowing the robot to adapt to how the human behaves when interacting with the robot. It is hypothesized that a speed increase can result from the robot augmenting the accuracy. The feasibility of the approach is validated on a positioning task where the robot controls degrees of freedom which have repeatable motion, and the human adapts motion in the complementary degrees of freedom. The approach is shown to be computationally suited to online use, it converges as the human and robot mutually adapt, and can increase the movement speed, although thorough human studies are needed in future work.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマンロボット協調把持におけるロボットの精度と速度向上を考慮した人間感覚運動モデルの適応
llm.tldr_ja: 確率的最適制御問題とFittsの法則からの時間的制約を適応させ、人間とロボットの協調動作を一致させるオンライン処理に適した手法を提案し、位置決めタスクで検証した。
llm.problem: 従来のロボット軌道計画手法は人間の動作に適応する時間的制約を考慮していない点。
llm.method: タスク制約からの最終状態制約を持つ確率的最適制御問題と、Fittsの法則からの時間的制約を適応させ、再帰的最小二乗法でパラメータを推定する。
llm.result: オンライン利用に適しており、人間とロボットが相互に適応するにつれて収束し、将来的な人間による詳細な研究が必要であるものの移動速度を向上できることを示した。
llm.limitation: 将来の研究として詳細な人間による研究が必要である
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボット協調

2611.02173.title: Directional Bounded-Confidence Cucker-Smale Flocking
2611.02173.abstract: This paper introduces a directional bounded-confidence extension of the Cucker--Smale (CS) flocking model that decomposes pairwise relative velocities into independent radial and tangential channels within the instantaneous line-of-sight frame. Gating these components via compactly supported kernels creates a time-varying, state-dependent, matrix-weighted interaction that strictly generalizes classical scalar CS alignment. We establish an exact energy-dissipation identity with conserved mean velocity and prove exponential velocity consensus under a sliding-window persistent excitation (PE) condition formulated directly on the disagreement subspace. Furthermore, we derive a CS bounded-diameter criterion separating metric decay from aggregate directional coercivity, along with a cluster convergence guarantee. Simulations validate the exact dissipation balance and demonstrate that directional gating successfully restores global alignment in scenarios where traditional isotropic tied-confidence laws remain polarized.

llm.title_ja: 方向性付き有界信頼Cucker-Smale群れモデル
llm.tldr_ja: ペアの相対速度を半径方向と接線方向に分解し、有界なサポートを持つカーネルでゲーティングを行うことで古典的なスカラーCS整列を一般化した方向性付き有界信頼Cucker-Smale群れモデルを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の等方的な結びつきを持つ信頼則が特定のシナリオで分極状態に陥る点。
llm.method: 瞬時の視線フレーム内で独立した半径方向および接線方向のチャネルに相対速度を分解し、状態依存の行列重み付き相互作用を構築する。
llm.result: 正確なエネルギー散逸則の確立と、スライドウィンドウ持続励振条件の下での指数関数的速度合意の証明に成功し、方向性ゲーティングが大域的整列を復元することを示した。

2611.02171.title: GoalDex: Learning Image-Goal-Conditioned Policies for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
2611.02171.abstract: Dexterous in-hand manipulation is commonly formulated around explicit object pose estimation, yet reliable pose tracking is challenging under severe hand-object occlusions and often requires object-specific supervision. This dependence creates a bottleneck between perception and control that can limit robustness and scalability. We present an end-to-end visuomotor framework for dexterous in-hand reorientation that operates on RGB observations and proprioception without intermediate pose estimation. Our approach jointly learns visual representations and control policies through behavior distillation from privileged state teachers and auxiliary reconstruction objectives. Furthermore, we introduce image-goal-conditioned reorientation, allowing desired object configurations to be specified directly through images rather than canonical pose representations. We evaluate our approach across a diverse set of object geometries and instances in simulation, where it consistently outperforms pose-based methods and policies built on pretrained visual encoders. Finally, we demonstrate direct sim-to-real transfer of a single image-goal-conditioned policy across five real-world objects, showing that accurate dexterous reorientation can be achieved without explicit pose estimation. For videos and code release, please refer to the project website: https://rffr.leggedrobotics.com/works/goaldex/

llm.title_ja: GoalDex: 器用なインハンド操作のための画像目標条件付きポリシーの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的なポーズ推定を必要とせず、RGB観測と固有受容感覚に基づいて視覚的表現と制御ポリシーを共同学習する、器用なインハンド再方向付けのエンドツーエンド視覚運動フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 器用なインハンド操作は明示的な物体ポーズ推定に依存することが多いが、深刻なオクルージョン下での信頼性の高いポーズ追跡は困難でありスケーラビリティが制限される点。
llm.method: 特権的状態ティーチャーからの行動模倣と補助的再構成目的により、視覚表現と制御ポリシーを共同で学習し、画像を介して目標物体構成を指定できるようにする。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて多様な物体ジオメトリで既存手法を上回り、単一のポリシーを5つの実世界物体へ直接Sim2Real転移することに成功した。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習

2611.02160.title: Value Forcing: Aligning Return Distributions at All Noise Levels
2611.02160.abstract: Learning accurate value functions is central to reinforcement learning (RL), yet remains challenging because supervision is limited and indirect: ground-truth values are unavailable, and each transition in the data only provides an immediate reward that can be used to construct bootstrapped targets as supervision. This challenge is particularly pronounced when data is limited or reward signals are sparse, as is common in real-world applications such as robotics. We argue that the key to accurate value learning in this limited data regime is extracting richer learning signals from the available data. In this paper, we introduce Value Forcing, a new approach that uses flow matching to estimate return distributions and enables accurate value learning from limited data. Our key insight is that we can extract richer learning signals by enforcing Bellman consistency at every noise level. Empirically, Value Forcing improves the accuracy of estimating the return distribution, and prevents the distribution from collapsing to a single value, as occurs with prior methods. We instantiate Value Forcing with two practical value-learning algorithms: VF, an actor-critic method, and IVF, an implicit value-learning method. We evaluate both algorithms across $26$ long-horizon tasks in the offline RL setting and find that they outperform prior value-learning methods, with particularly large gains when data is limited. Our project website is available at https://chongyi-zheng.github.io/value-forcing.

llm.title_ja: Value Forcing: すべてのノイズレベルにおけるリターン分布の整列
llm.tldr_ja: フローマッチングを用いてリターン分布を推定し、すべてのノイズレベルでベルマン整合性を強制することで限られたデータから正確な価値学習を実現する「Value Forcing」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボット工学などの実世界応用においてデータが限られていたり報酬信号がまばらである場合、監督が制限的かつ間接的であるため正確な価値関数の学習が困難である点。
llm.method: フローマッチングを用いてリターン分布を推定し、すべてのノイズレベルでベルマン整合性を強制して豊富な学習信号を抽出する。
llm.result: 26の長期タスクのオフラインRL設定において従来の手法を上回り、特にデータが限られている場合に大きな性能向上を達成した。

2611.02140.title: History-Aware Force Sensing and Tunable Stiffness in a Pneumatic Kresling Origami Cell
2611.02140.abstract: Mechanical hysteresis and pneumatic loading complicate contact force estimation from deformation measurements in soft robots. This work presents a 3D-printed polyether block amide (PEBA) Kresling cell with magnetic angular sensing that supports three operating modes: force sensing at zero gauge pressure, force sensing with tunable stiffness under gauge positive pressure, and self-sensing actuation under negative gauge pressure. A multiscale gated recurrent unit (GRU) network estimates contact force from angular histories to account for the the combined effects of geometric deformation and material response. At zero gauge pressure, the model achieves a test RMSE of 0.76~N. Positive gauge pressure approximately doubles the average axial loading stiffness at +20~kPa over the first 3~mm of compression, while pressure-specific models maintain RMSEs below 0.93~N. Under negative gauge pressure, an energy-based compensation model enables contact force estimation using the the model trained at zero gauge pressure, achieving RMSEs of 1.66--2.10~N under quasi-static conditions. These results demonstrate a compact approach to combining force feedback, tunable axial stiffness, and self-sensing actuation in soft origami systems.

llm.title_ja: 空気圧式Kresling折り紙セルにおける履歴を考慮した力覚センシングと可変剛性
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学的変形と材料応答の複合効果に対応するため、マルチスケールGRUネットワークを用いて角度履歴から接触力を推定する、磁気角度センシングを備えた3Dプリント製Kresling折り紙セルを開発した。
llm.problem: 機械的ヒステリシスと空気圧負荷により、柔軟ロボットの変形測定から接触力を正確に推定することが複雑になる点。
llm.method: マルチスケールGRUネットワークを用いて、角度履歴から接触力を推定し、異るゲージ圧力下での動作モードを実現する。
llm.result: ゼロゲージ圧力下でテストRMSE 0.76 Nを達成し、正圧により軸方向負荷剛性が約2倍になり、負圧下でもエネルギーベース補正モデルにより高精度な力推定が可能となった。

2611.02101.title: When Delay Meets Drift: Physical Safety of Robot Foundation Models Is a Cross-Layer Problem
2611.02101.abstract: Robot foundation models now act in a closed loop, yet their safety is evaluated one variation at a time: robustness benchmarks perturb the scene while assuming instantaneous inference, and real-time execution methods study inference delay in nominal scenes. We argue that physical safety is not a property of the model alone, but emerges from how variations in the physical environment, the model, the computing platform, and execution interact in closed loop. We formalize this as cross-layer variation propagation across these system layers and use an interaction contrast to measure when joint variation creates more risk than the sum of its parts. In 4,000 paired closed-loop episodes of the pi0.5 vision-language-action model on LIBERO, a 400 ms inference delay raises the safety-violation rate by 3.5 percentage points under the training viewpoint but by 37 percentage points under a 60-degree camera shift: 33.5 percentage points (95% CI: 25-43) more than the two effects combined. We close with a research agenda toward predictable physical intelligence: predicting when variation becomes risk, and adapting compute, power, and control accordingly.

llm.title_ja: 遅延とドリフトが出会うとき：ロボット基盤モデルの物理的安全性はクロスレイヤーの問題である
llm.tldr_ja: 物理環境、モデル、計算プラットフォーム、実行の各レイヤー間の変動伝播をクロスレイヤー変動として定式化し、推論遅延とカメラ視点シフトが安全違反率に与える相乗的なリスクを実証した。
llm.problem: ロボット基盤モデルの安全性が、瞬間的推論を仮定した頑健性ベンチマークや名目上のシーンでの遅延評価など、個別の変動要因ごとにしか評価されていない点。
llm.method: システムレイヤー間を横断する変動伝播を定式化し、LIBERO環境におけるpi0.5モデルを用いた4,000組の閉ループエピソードで相互作用コントラストを測定する。
llm.result: 400msの推論遅延が、訓練視点では安全違反率を3.5%上昇させる一方で、60度のカメラシフト下では37%（期待値より33.5%多い）上昇させることを示した。

2611.02090.title: Local Solution Repair for Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery
2611.02090.abstract: Multi-robot systems in automated warehouses must efficiently attend to a constant stream of pickup-and-delivery tasks while avoiding collisions. Existing Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery (MAPD) solutions generate plans that are globally feasible but often locally inefficient. In large-scale, long-horizon deployments, these inefficiencies, such as robots backtracking from target goal locations and idling in congested areas, accumulate over time and degrade performance. This paper contributes Local Solution Repair (LSR), a goal replanning approach that detects suboptimal behaviors at run-time and locally improves plans to reduce conflict between agents. We demonstrate the utility of our approach by repairing solutions generated by state-of-the-art MAPD baselines, M2M and LNS-PBS. Our results in long-horizon warehouse simulations over three environments show upwards of 5.9% improvement in task throughput over current state-of-the-art methods by reducing the number of suboptimal instances by ~36k or by 14.6% with minor additional computation time.

llm.title_ja: マルチエージェント・ピックアップ＆デリバリーのための局所解修復
llm.tldr_ja: 自動倉庫における長期運用での非効率性を改善するため、実行時に最適でない挙動を検出し、エージェント間の競合を減らすために局所的に計画を改善する目標再計画アプローチ「Local Solution Repair (LSR)」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のMAPDソリューションが生成する大域的に実行可能な計画が、バックトラックや混雑エリアでのアイドルなどの局所的非効率性を蓄積し性能を低下させる点。
llm.method: 実行時に最適でない挙動を検出し、計画を局所的に改善してエージェント間の競合を減らす目標再計画アプローチを用いる。
llm.result: 3つの環境における長期倉庫シミュレーションにおいて、最適でないインスタンスを約36k件削減することで、タスクスループットを5.9%以上向上させた。

2611.02076.title: Scene-Adaptive Readout and Decoding in Diffusion Driving VLAs
2611.02076.abstract: Diffusion driving vision-language-action models repeatedly execute the backbone at every denoising stage, incurring substantial inference cost, while it remains unclear whether all scenes require the same decoding computation. To distinguish when a trajectory becomes readable from how much further refinement it requires, we analyze trajectory readout across network depth and decoding progress. We identify a depth-decoding dissociation in which late-layer representations already support useful trajectory readout after the first forward sweep, whereas early-layer representations benefit more from continued decoding. We further find that both the preferred readout layer and decoding depth vary across scenes. Based on these observations, we propose a scene-adaptive readout and decoding framework. A scene-conditioned readout MoE adaptively weights and combines trajectory predictions from layer-specific late-layer representations after a single backbone sweep, while an adaptive decoding policy applies additional native refinement only when required by the scene. We evaluate our framework on two diffusion driving VLAs across the Waymo E2E and nuScenes benchmarks. Our method improves validation RFS by up to 0.56 while also improving test performance, and achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to $6.0\times$ on Waymo E2E, while consistently reducing trajectory error on nuScenes. These results demonstrate that scene-level readout and decoding allocation improves planning quality while avoiding unnecessary decoding. Our code is available at https://github.com/sjyu001/SARD

llm.title_ja: 拡散駆動型VLAにおけるシーン適応型読み出しとデコーディング
llm.tldr_ja: シーンごとのトラジェクトリ読み出しの深さとデコーディングの進捗の乖離を分析し、必要なシーンでのみ追加のネイティブ洗練を適用するシーン適応型の読み出しおよびデコーディングフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 拡散駆動型ビジョン言語アクションモデルがすべてのノイズ除去段階でバックボーンを繰り返し実行し多大な推論コストを伴う一方、全シーンで同一のデコーディング計算が必要か不明である点。
llm.method: シーン条件付き読み出しMixture of Experts（MoE）により単一のバックボーンスイープ後にレイヤー固有の表現を重み付け・結合し、適応的デコーディングポリシーで必要な場合のみ追加の洗練を行う。
llm.result: Waymo E2EおよびnuScenesベンチマークにおいてバリデーションRFSを最大0.56向上させ、Waymo E2Eで最大6.0倍のエンドツーエンドの高速化を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.02073.title: Back to the Future: Predicting Long-Horizon Dynamics with Retrospective Correction for Disturbance-Aware Retrieval
2611.02073.abstract: Retrieving objects from densely packed storage requires anticipating how contact disturbs surrounding objects when limited clearance prevents lifting the target over clutter. However, contact can propagate beyond the target's immediate neighbors, while accumulated prediction errors make learned dynamics unreliable over long planning horizons. We introduce DARE (Disturbance-Aware REtrieval), a geometry-aware relational dynamics framework that uses retrospective correction to improve long-horizon prediction for disturbance-aware retrieval. DARE encodes compact object descriptors and predicts action-conditioned disturbance propagation through object-level message passing. When a sparse observation becomes available, a learned corrector uses the prediction discrepancy to amend an earlier predicted state and reruns the intervening dynamics, propagating the correction through the predicted contact chain. These predictions guide a receding-horizon planner that balances retrieval progress against displacement and rotation of surrounding objects, permitting necessary contact while discouraging harmful disturbance. Experiments in planar and RoboCasa environments evaluate long-horizon prediction, generalization, and robustness for disturbance-aware retrieval in dense clutter. See our project website: https://the-back-to-the-future.github.io
2611.02073.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ICRA 2027

llm.title_ja: バック・トゥ・ザ・フューチャー：外乱認識型検索のための遡及的補正を用いた長期ダイナミクス予測
llm.tldr_ja: 密集した環境でのオブジェクト検索において、予測の不一致を利用して過去の状態を修正し動的接触連鎖に伝播させる、遡及的補正を用いた幾何学認識型関係ダイナミクスフレームワーク「DARE」を提案した。
llm.problem: 限られた隙間のために目標物を上の空間へ持ち上げることができない密集したストレージからの物体検索において、接触の伝播や蓄積された予測誤差により学習済みダイナミクスが長期計画において信頼できなくなる点。
llm.method: コンパクトなオブジェクト記述子をコード化し、オブジェクトレベルのメッセージパッシングを通じて行動条件付き外乱伝播を予測し、学習済み補正器で過去の予測状態を修正する。
llm.result: 平面的環境およびRoboCasa環境での実験により、密集したクラッタにおける外乱認識型検索の長期予測、汎用性、頑健性が評価された。

2611.02056.title: Do Embodied VLMs Actually Use Their Scene-Graph Memory?
2611.02056.abstract: Embodied agents that answer questions about their route need a memory of what they saw, and scene graphs are a natural form for it. A vision-language model (VLM) can receive such a graph as text or through a graph encoder, but accuracy alone cannot show whether the graph holds the episode's facts, reaches the model, or is actually relied on. In this diagnostic study, we introduce a graph-swap test for the last of these: each episode is given another episode's graph, and we count how many answers change. On an embodied question-answering benchmark with routes through two to seven rooms, we use it to compare ways of delivering scene-graph memory to a fine-tuned VLM. As text, the memory is used strongly, adding 30 points on route questions. As a graph, it is not, and we trace why: the encoder preserves the information, but standard pooled and late fusion discard it. Giving each node its own input token recovers part of it, a gain of 8.3 points on route questions that the swap test confirms comes from the graph. The test also exposes a shortcut that accuracy hides: when the same facts appear in the text, the model ignores its graph. The test thus offers a cheap check of whether a VLM uses its scene-graph memory, and our analysis points to how that memory should be delivered.

llm.title_ja: 身体性VLMは実際にシーン・グラフ・メモリを使用しているか？
llm.tldr_ja: ファインチューニングされたVLMへのシーン・グラフ・メモリの提供方法を評価するため、エピソード間でグラフを入れ替えて回答の変化を数える「グラフスワップテスト」を導入し診断を行った。
llm.problem: VLMがテキストやグラフエンコーダーを通じてシーン・グラフを受け取れるものの、単なる精度評価ではモデルが実際にグラフの事実を依存して使用しているか判断できない点。
llm.method: エピソードごとに別のエピソードのグラフを与えるグラフスワップテストを導入し、回答の変化数をカウントして評価する。
llm.result: テキストとしてのメモリは強く利用される一方、標準的なプーディングや後期融合ではグラフ情報が破棄されること、またテキストに同じ事実がある場合にモデルがグラフを無視するショートカットを露わにした。

2611.02049.title: Reinforcement Learning in High-Energy Physics: A Survey from Accelerator Control to Theory Exploration
2611.02049.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a machine learning paradigm in which an agent learns a decision-making policy by interacting with an environment, guided by a scalar reward rather than explicit supervision. Supervised and unsupervised learning have become indispensable tools in high-energy physics (HEP), but they learn from fixed datasets, whereas many HEP tasks are closed-loop decisions: the data an algorithm observes depend on its choices, the feedback is sparse or delayed, and the objective is often measured on a real machine or in a stochastic simulation, not by a differentiable model. This survey reviews the application of RL to such tasks: accelerator control and feedback, data quality monitoring, jet grooming, clustering, and representation, charged particle tracking, beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) and string model building, detector design, trigger control, analysis, and formal quantum field theory computation. It provides a self-contained introduction to the underlying RL methods, from model-free and model-based to multi-agent, offline, inverse, and bandit approaches, reviews each domain against its traditional methods, and summarizes the head-to-head comparisons. The applications range from policies deployed on real accelerators and evaluated on recorded collision data to exploratory studies in formal theory. RL is most advantageous for repeated tasks with a fast simulator, decisions inside fast control loops, operation under faults and corrupted measurements, physics-based rewards in place of labels, and sequential discrete constructions with a reusable policy, while Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and differentiable methods remain competitive elsewhere. We conclude with the open challenges that recur across domains, including reward design, sim-to-real transfer, safety, the lack of shared benchmarks, and the statistical validity of policy-driven decisions.

llm.title_ja: 高エネルギー物理学における強化学習：加速器制御から理論探索まで
llm.tldr_ja: 高エネルギー物理学（HEP）における加速器制御、データ品質監視、荷電粒子追跡、検出器設計などの閉ループ意思決定タスクに対する強化学習の応用を包括的にレビューした。
llm.problem: 多くのHEPタスクが固定データセットから学習する従来の教師なし・教師あり学習の枠組みを超え、アルゴリズムの選択に観測データが依存する閉ループ意思決定である点。
llm.method: モデルフリー、モデルベース、マルチエージェント、オフライン、逆強化学習、バンディット手法に至るまで、基礎となる強化学習手法の自己完結型の紹介と各ドメインの伝統的手法との比較を行う。
llm.result: 高速シミュレータを持つ反復タスクや高速制御ループ内の決定などにおける強化学習の優位性をまとめ、報酬設計やSim2Realなどの共通するオープンな課題を結論づけた。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.02034.title: 4D Triangle Splatting Reconstruction of Dynamic Endoscopic Scenes from Monocular Videos
2611.02034.abstract: Robust 4D reconstruction of deformable endoscopic scenes from monocular videos remains challenging due to non-rigid tissue deformation, illumination changes, occlusions, and unknown camera trajectories. Reliable dynamic reconstruction of endoscopies could significantly enhance visualization, diagnostic accuracy and intraoperative guidance of minimally invasive procedures. We propose SurgicalTS, a self-supervised triangle-splatting framework for dynamic endoscopic scene reconstruction from static monocular cameras. The scene is represented by a canonical set of triangles jointly optimized with a deformation network. We introduce a quaternion-based deformation model, an improved color parametrization, spatio-temporal priors, and a redefined initialization strategy that improves completeness under occlusions. Extensive evaluation on challenging in-vivo endoscopy videos from diverse procedures shows that SurgicalTS successfully models soft-tissue deformations and tool-tissue interactions over time, while consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our method also reduces training times while maintaining competitive geometric and photometric accuracy results, highlighting the effectiveness of quaternion-based deformation modelling with physical consistency for robust and efficient 4D reconstruction of endoscopic scenes.

llm.title_ja: 単眼ビデオからの動的内視鏡シーンの4D三角形スプラッティング再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 非剛体組織変形やオクルージョンに対応するため、変形ネットワークと共同最適化されるカノニカルな三角形集合を用いて動的内視鏡シーンを自己教師あり学習で再構成する「SurgicalTS」を提案した。
llm.problem: 非剛体組織の変形、照明変化、オクルージョン、未知のカメラ軌道のため、単眼ビデオからの変形可能な内視鏡シーンの頑健な4D再構成が困難である点。
llm.method: カノニカルな三角形のセットと変形ネットワークを共同最適化し、四元数ベースの変形モデル、色パラメータ化、時空間事前知識を導入する。
llm.result: 多様な手技からのインビボ内視鏡ビデオにおいて、軟組織の変形やツールと組織の相互作用を正確にモデル化し、従来手法を上回る再構成性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 三角形スプラッティング

2611.02026.title: Reconstruction as Spatial Evaluation: Diagnosing Cross-View Spatial Intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models
2611.02026.abstract: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. To bridge this gap, we introduce RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark centered on multi-view 3D scene reconstruction across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor environments. Given real multi-view images and target-object queries, LVLMs are required to jointly predict oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared, camera-anchored metric coordinate frame. Reconstructions are evaluated along two complementary axes: Structure for relative layout and Metric for physical scale and camera-anchored placement. Nine atomic spatial QA tasks, grouped into Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, probe spatial capabilities involved in joint reconstruction. Offline navigation extends evaluation to path planning. Evaluation of 18 frontier LVLMs reveals a consistent gap between relative scene structure and metric reconstruction; even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric. Tracing this gap, diagnostic analyses link atomic spatial capabilities to reconstruction quality and show that relational consistency alone does not ensure metric accuracy. Experiments with 3D map injection further separate scene construction from path planning, revealing how these geometric errors limit navigation success. Finally, spatial fine-tuning yields broad transfer across both spatial and general vision-language benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: 空間評価としての再構成：大規模ビジョン言語モデルにおけるクロスビュー空間知能の診断
llm.tldr_ja: マルチビュー3Dシーン再構成に基づくベンチマーク「RECONSPATIAL」を導入し、屋内・卓上・屋外環境における大規模ビジョン言語モデル（LVLM）の空間知能を構造と精度の軸から評価した。
llm.problem: 静的ベンチマークが孤立した空間的判断を評価する一方、インタラクティブな身体的評価は知覚と計画、制御などを複合的に扱うためギャップが存在する点。
llm.method: マルチビュー画像とクエリから、共有のカメラアンカー付き座標系で向き付き3Dバウンディングボックスを共同予測させ、構造（相対配置）とメトリック（物理スケール）の2軸で評価する。
llm.result: 18の最先端LVLMの評価により、相対シーン構造とメトリック再構成の間に一貫したギャップが存在することが明らかになり、空間的ファインチューニングの有効性を示した。

2611.01958.title: Answering Without Arriving: An Evidence Audit for Embodied Question Answering
2611.01958.abstract: Embodied question answering asks an agent to navigate, observe, and then answer questions about what it saw, yet answer accuracy alone cannot tell whether any of this happened. A plausible answer can come from the question, the room label, or the answer choices, and a correct answer does not show that the supporting observation was ever made. We present a multi-room benchmark whose 200 test episodes and 800 questions are stratified by route extent, with an evaluation ladder that holds the questions fixed while varying only the evidence supplied to the answerer, from text-only probes through closed-loop agents to replay of the reference trajectory. Questions are generated from symbolic records of rooms, visible objects, and frames, so every answer can be traced to the observations that support it. A closed-loop vision-language agent reaches no target in 200 episodes yet answers 45.5% of questions, within 0.1 points of the same model given no images; replaying the reference trajectory raises the same model to 57.4%, so the evidence exists along the route but is not gathered. A family-level audit then shows that access to evidence is not the same as use of it. Four of eight families are largely answerable from text, one cites frames that cannot establish its own answer, and the oracle conditions reach 59.5% on Rooms-visited by counting the supplied images. Evidence acquisition, answer coverage, and shortcut sensitivity must therefore be established before an accuracy gain can be credited to memory.

llm.title_ja: 到着せずに答える：身体性質問応答のための証拠監査
llm.tldr_ja: ルートの広さに応じて階層化されたマルチルームベンチマークを構築し、質問を固定したまま提供する証拠を変化させる評価ラダーを用いて、身体性質問応答におけるエージェントの証拠収集とメモリ利用の実態を監査した。
llm.problem: 身体性質問応答において、正解が得られてもそれが対応する観察結果に基づいているとは限らず、回答の正確性だけではエージェントが実際に経路上の情報を収集してメモリを活用しているか判断できない点。
llm.method: ルートの広さで階層化されたベンチマークを用い、テキストのみのプローブから閉ループエージェント、参照軌道の再生へと提供する証拠を変化させる評価ラダーで監査を行う。
llm.result: 閉ループ視覚言語エージェントが目標に全く到達しなくても画像なしモデルと同等の正解率を達成することを示し、メモリに正当性を認める前に証拠の獲得やショートカット感度を確立する必要があることを示した。

2611.01934.title: TriPhysBench: Evaluating Physical Intelligence for Embodied Agents
2611.01934.abstract: Embodied agents need physical intelligence to understand their surroundings through physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning. These capabilities must work together to interpret events and make quantitative judgments. Existing benchmarks advance physical understanding and general-purpose tool use, yet the coordination of these capabilities in physical scenarios remains insufficiently characterized. Inspired by Popper's Three Worlds, we introduce TriPhysBench, a benchmark of 410 questions from 200 videos that brings physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning into a shared evaluation setting. Its measurement-grounded and knowledge-grounded subtasks impose complementary demands on obtaining observations and acquiring external specifications, then applying them to quantitative problems. Among six representative vision-language models, the best achieves an answer accuracy of only 50.38%, revealing limited performance on tasks that require these capabilities to work together. We further introduce TriPhys, a framework that learns a unified policy for physical perception, knowledge retrieval, and quantitative reasoning from complete tool-integrated trajectories. The policy uses intermediate reasoning to guide retrieval and computation, then incorporates tool feedback into subsequent physical inference. On 110 questions from videos excluded from training, TriPhys improves answer and solution scores across three Qwen configurations, with a 17.7% relative gain in answer accuracy for TriPhys-27B over its Qwen3.6-27B backbone. This work provides a benchmark and a learning pathway toward embodied agents that move beyond recognizing events to understanding and reasoning about the physical processes behind them.

llm.title_ja: TriPhysBench：身体性エージェントのための物理知能の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的知能を評価するためのベンチマーク「TriPhysBench」と、完全なツール統合軌跡から物理知能の方策を学習するフレームワーク「TriPhys」を提案し、複数能力の協調における課題と改善を示した。
llm.problem: 物理的知能を構成する知覚・知識検索・推論の各能力が物理シナリオにおいてどのように協調するかに関する特徴づけが不十分であること。
llm.method: Popperの3つの世界にインスパイアされた410問のベンチマーク「TriPhysBench」と、ツール統合軌跡から統一された方策を学習するフレームワーク「TriPhys」の提案。
llm.result: 6つの代表的なVLMの最高正答率は50.38%にとどまり、TriPhysはQwenバックボーンに対して正答率で17.7%の相対的改善を達成した。

2611.01844.title: OpenNWM: A Generalist Navigation World Model with Latent Action Pretraining
2611.01844.abstract: Navigation world models predict future observations conditioned on navigation actions to support planning, but their generalization across real-world environments remains constrained by the limited coverage of action-labeled data. Action-free navigation videos provide diverse visual experience, yet lack the recorded actions required for action-conditioned training. We introduce OpenNWM, a generalist navigation world model with latent action pretraining. It learns universal latent actions from large-scale action-free videos through visual prediction pretraining, and further aligns them with physical motions via action-conditioned post-training. To support video pretraining, we curate NavAnywhere, a large-scale action-free navigation video dataset comprising 17.5 million visual observations from 15 heterogeneous sources. It captures navigation by ground robots, humans, and drones, with diverse viewpoints and motion patterns across five broad scene types: residential areas, public and commercial spaces, urban settings, parks, and natural landscapes. Experiments demonstrate improved visual prediction on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, together with improved navigation performance. These results show that latent-action pretraining enables diverse, action-free videos to improve dynamics learning and generalization for open-world navigation.

llm.title_ja: OpenNWM：潜在行動事前学習を備えた汎用ナビゲーション世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模な行動なしナビゲーション動画からビジュアル予測事前学習を通じて普遍的な潜在行動を学習し、行動条件付きポストトレーニングで物理的運動に整合させる汎用ナビゲーション世界モデル「OpenNWM」を提案した。
llm.problem: 実世界環境におけるナビゲーション世界モデルの汎化が、行動ラベル付きデータのカバレッジの限界によって制約されていること。
llm.method: 大規模な行動なしナビゲーション動画を用いた視覚予測事前学習により普遍的な潜在行動を学習し、行動条件付きポストトレーニングで物理的運動に整合させる手法。
llm.result: ドメイン内およびドメイン外のベンチマークでの視覚予測の改善と、ナビゲーション性能の向上が示された。

2611.01814.title: Control Barrier Functions for Safety-Aware Latent-Space Motion Planning
2611.01814.abstract: Latent-space path planning (LSPP) compresses the configuration space of a robotic manipulator into a compact, differentiable manifold learned by a variational autoencoder, enabling fast gradient-based planning without explicit inverse kinematics. Existing LSPP frameworks enforce obstacle avoidance with a binary collision classifier, whose saturated gradients near obstacle boundaries and lack of temporal structure cause the optimizer to stall and provide no forward-invariance guarantee. We replace the classifier with a neural control barrier function (CBF) learned directly in the latent space. The barrier is trained with a three-term objective that combines safe and unsafe sign constraints with a discrete-time decrease condition evaluated on transitions of an obstacle-blind nominal planner, and it is enforced at planning time by a closed-form, first-order correction that projects each goal-directed latent step back onto the CBF constraint. On a 7-DoF Franka Panda manipulator, the CBF planner achieves a 75.6\% success rate on a fixed-obstacle task, 12.0 percentage points above the best of 35 tuned classifier configurations, and 83.8\% on a multi-position task. A sweep of the decay rate $α$ characterizes the safety--performance trade-off, with the best operating points in $α\in [0.10, 0.20]$. In a fully general random-obstacle setting, success drops to 33.0\%, which we trace to covariate shift between the obstacle-blind training transitions and the states visited by the corrected planner.

llm.title_ja: 安全性考慮型潜在空間モーションプランニングのための制御バリア関数
llm.tldr_ja: 変分オートエンコーダで学習されたコンパクトな潜在空間において、二値衝突分類器をニューラル制御バリア関数（CBF）に置き換えることで、安全性を保証する高速な勾配ベースのパスプランニング手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の潜在空間パスプランニング（LSPP）は、二値衝突分類器に起因して最適化が停滞し、前方不変性の保証がないこと。
llm.method: 分類器を潜在空間で直接学習されたニューラル制御バリア関数（CBF）に置き換え、計画時に閉形式の一次補正により目標指向の潜在ステップをCBF制約に射影する。
llm.result: 7軸のFranka Pandaマニピュレータを用いた固定障害物タスクで75.6%の成功率を達成し、最良の分類器構成を12.0ポイント上回った。
llm.limitation: 一般的なランダム障害物の設定では、訓練時の遷移と補正された方策が訪れる状態との間の共変量シフトにより成功率が33.0%に低下した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.01783.title: OCBI: Order-Sensitive Cross-Branch Interaction for Image Manipulation Localization
2611.01783.abstract: Image manipulation localization combines semantic structure with forensic traces to identify modified pixels. Within-branch spatial mixing and RGB-guided cross-branch mixing can produce different messages when composed in opposite orders. We propose OCBI, an extension of Co-Transformers that models the discrepancy between these two composition orders for localization. A local cross-branch fusion module uses the commutator of RGB-guided cross-attention and forensic self-attention to add a learnable signed correction to feature transfer. Pixelwise adaptive multiscale aggregation then combines spatial contexts before prediction. OCBI uses the Co-Transformers backbone and supervision. We compare OCBI with retrained Co-Transformers using CASIA-only task training, a 50-epoch budget, and final-epoch evaluation. Across five clean test datasets, OCBI achieves a macro PixelF1 of 0.5773, exceeding the baseline by 0.43 percentage points. Under JPEG compression, Gaussian blur, and resizing on three datasets, its average PixelF1 over 21 dataset-transformation conditions exceeds the baseline by 0.95 percentage points.

llm.title_ja: OCBI：画像改ざん局所化のための順序依存クロスブランチ相互作用
llm.tldr_ja: RGB誘導クロスアテンションとフォレンジック自己アテンションの交換子を用いた局所クロスブランチ融合モジュールにより、2つの構成順序の不一致をモデル化する画像改ざん局所化手法「OCBI」を提案した。
llm.problem: ブランチ内の空間ミキシングとRGB誘導クロスブランチミキシングが、逆の順序で合成された場合に異なるメッセージを生成する可能性があり、その不一致のモデル化が必要であること。
llm.method: RGB誘導クロスアテンションとフォレンジック自己アテンションの交換子を用いて特徴転送に学習可能な符号付き補正を加える局所クロスブランチ融合モジュールの提案。
llm.result: 5つのクリーンなテストデータセットでマクロPixelF1が0.5773を達成し、ベースラインを0.43パーセンテージポイント上回った。

2611.01759.title: Teleoperation System for Service Robots using Virtual Reality Headset and Pose Estimation
2611.01759.abstract: This paper presents a teleoperation system for service robots that integrates human pose estimation with virtual reality (VR) to enable intuitive remote control. By using the Mediapipe framework for 2D pose detection and extending it with RGB-D data from the Intel RealSense D455 camera, a comprehensive 3D human pose estimation is achieved. This data is then mapped to the robot's kinematics, allowing the operator to control the robot's movements naturally. A VR interface was developed to provide an immersive perspective, enhancing the operator's situational awareness. Real-world experiments were conducted using the CHARMIE service robot to validate the system's effectiveness in tasks involving object manipulation. While the current system successfully demonstrates the potential of VR-based teleoperation, challenges remain in accurately capturing certain joint angles (e.g., wrist yaw) and ensuring precise mapping between human and robot movements. Future work includes the integration of inertial measurement units (IMUs) for improved rotational tracking and the implementation of more advanced control algorithms. Overall, this research contributes to the development of more intuitive and effective teleoperation systems for service robots, facilitating their deployment in complex and dynamic environments. This work further introduces a novel approach to teleoperation by combining RGB-D sensing with an innovative algorithm for real-time joint angle computation using Mediapipe, enhancing the precision of human-robot motion mapping and enabling immersive control through a VR interface. These contributions represent significant advancements in the field of human-robot interaction, particularly for service robot applications.

llm.title_ja: 仮想現実ヘッドセットと姿勢推定を用いたサービスロボット向け遠隔操作システム
llm.tldr_ja: MediapipeとRGB-Dカメラを統合して3D人間の姿勢推定を行い、ロボットの運動学にマッピングすることで直感的な遠隔制御とVRによる没入型の状況認識を実現するシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: サービスロボットの遠隔操作において、直感的なリモートコントロールと没入型の状況認識を両立させること。
llm.method: MediapipeフレームワークとIntel RealSense D455カメラを組み合わせた3D姿勢推定データをロボットの運動学にマッピングし、VRインターフェースを統合する。
llm.result: CHARMIEサービスロボットを用いた実世界実験により、物体操作タスクにおけるシステムの有効性が検証された。
llm.limitation: 手首のヨー角などの特定の関節角度の正確なキャプチャや、人間とロボットの動きの正確なマッピングに課題が残る。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.01748.title: CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control
2611.01748.abstract: Humanoid controllers need the ability to yield to external forces while retaining the capacity to resume their original tasks. However, tracking objectives penalize the deviations needed for yielding, while relaxing tracking goals persistently can make task recovery harder. Existing approaches often rely on task-specific interaction command interfaces or constructed compliant motion data and reference trajectories, limiting the direct reuse of their compliance-training mechanisms across different task interfaces. We introduce CompliantBot, a compliance-training framework for motion tracking and velocity-command locomotion. It preserves the original task inputs and requires no preconstructed compliant data or target trajectories. A state-dependent interaction force field couples applied loads to the robot's motion, enabling local articulation and whole-body movement to change the forces experienced. A complementary force-magnitude reward encourages lower interaction loads, while task rewards are downweighted during loading and restored after release to coordinate yielding and task resumption. The trained policies use task inputs and proprioceptive history without explicit external-force measurements. Across both task interfaces, CompliantBot yields farther under constant pulls and experiences lower spring interaction loads than matched baselines, while resuming task tracking after force removal. CompliantBot achieves the highest task completion among the compared methods under stronger pulls. Power evaluations further show that CompliantBot has the lowest mean joint mechanical power among the compared methods. Real-robot demonstrations further illustrate compliant responses through arm motion, stepping, and body reorientation.

llm.title_ja: CompliantBot：ヒューノイド制御のためのタスク間インターフェースを通じた全身コンプライアンスの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 事前構築されたコンプライアンスデータやターゲット軌道を必要とせず、状態依存の相互作用力場と補完的な力大きさ報酬を用いて、モーション追従と速度指令ロコモーションの両方で柔軟なコンプライアンスを実現するフレームワーク「CompliantBot」を提案した。
llm.problem: 追従目的が譲歩に必要な偏差をペナルティ化し、追従目標を永続的に緩和するとタスク回復が困難になること。
llm.method: 状態依存の相互作用力場を用いて外力をロボットの運動に結合し、力大きさ報酬とタスク報酬の重み付けを動的に調整する。
llm.result: 定常的な引っ張りに対してより遠くまで譲り、スプリング相互作用負荷を低減しつつ、力除去後のタスク追従再開を実現した。

2611.01729.title: ODE Policy: Robot Learning via Action Dynamics, Not Actions
2611.01729.abstract: Most robot policies, whether trained by imitation learning (IL) or reinforcement learning (RL), map observations to action values at discrete control steps and leave the continuity of physical motion to be learned implicitly. We propose ODE policy, which learns the dynamics of the action rather than the action itself. A neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) learns the vector field of the action by matching the integrated actions to the targets over short action chunks in IL and single control steps in RL. A lightweight diversity head captures multi-modal behavior by randomizing the direction of the field. At deployment, each action is integrated from the previous one, so the executed trajectory is continuous by construction. We evaluate it as a visuomotor policy, as the action head of vision-language-action (VLA) and world action models (WAMs), and as the actor of model-based RL against 14 baselines on unimanual, bimanual, dexterous, locomotion, and loco-manipulation tasks. In IL, against flow matching, it reaches 5.9$\times$ the success, 5.4$\times$ the generalization, and 3.9$\times$ the mode balance after one epoch, and generates actions 10.8$\times$ faster. It mostly moves more smoothly than human demonstrations. On 14 real-world tasks across single-arm, dual-arm, dexterous, and humanoid robots, it achieves the highest success rate. In RL, it further speeds up SuperMimic for humanoid motion tracking and smooths its actions. Efficient in learning, data, parameters, and execution, ODE policy offers a promising path to scaling robot learning.

llm.title_ja: ODE Policy：アクションではなく行動ダイナミクスを通じたロボット学習
llm.tldr_ja: アクションそのものではなくアクションのダイナミクスをニューラル常微分方程式（ODE）で学習し、実行軌跡を構築によって連続にする「ODE Policy」を提案し、多様なタスクで高い成功率と滑らかな動作を実現した。
llm.problem: 従来の方策は観測を離散的な制御ステップのアクション値にマッピングし、物理的運動の連続性を暗黙的に学習させるに留まっていること。
llm.method: ニューラル常微分方程式（ODE）を用いてアクションのベクトル場を学習し、デプロイ時に前のものから各アクションを積分する。
llm.result: 14の実世界タスクにおいて最高の成功率を達成し、模倣学習のフローマッチングと比較して1 epoch後に5.9倍の成功率を示した。

2611.01713.title: Route-Guided CBF-QP Repair for Safe Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.01713.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can generate task-oriented robot actions, but they do not guarantee safe execution in obstacle-rich manipulation scenes. Although CBF-QP safety filters can locally project unsafe actions into a safe set, such correction may push the robot away from the learned task trajectory and leave the VLA policy without a reliable recovery direction. We propose Route-Guided CBF-QP Repair, a post-hoc repair module that uses the short-horizon action chunk predicted by the VLA to detect blocked nominal trajectories and generate entry-exit-rejoin guidance around obstacles. The selected route is added to the CBF-QP objective as a soft guidance term, while the CBF safety constraint remains hard. On SafeLIBERO, our method improves collision avoidance, task success, and SafeSuccess compared with AEGIS. Our project page is available at GitHub.

llm.title_ja: 安全な視覚言語行動モデルのためのルート誘導型CBF-QP修復
llm.tldr_ja: VLAが予測する短期アクションチャンクを使用して障害物周囲の回避ルートを生成し、それをCBF-QPのソフト誘導項として追加することで、安全性を維持しつつタスク成功率を向上させる事後修復モジュールを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚言語行動モデル（VLA）は障害物の多い操作シーンにおいて安全な実行を保証できず、従来のCBF-QP安全性フィルタはタスク軌道からロボットを遠ざけてしまうこと。
llm.method: VLAが予測する短期アクションチャンクで遮断された名目軌道を検出し、障害物周囲の案内を生成してCBF-QPのソフトガイダンス項として追加する。
llm.result: SafeLIBEROにおいて、AEGISと比較して衝突回避、タスク成功率、SafeSuccessが向上した。

2611.01663.title: GatedVLA with Camera-Based Emergency Braking: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report
2611.01663.abstract: This report presents GatedVLA, our entry for the Physical AI AV (PAI-AV) track. Our learned vision-language-action (VLA) policy pairs the driving-pretrained Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B vision-language model with a layer-wise flow-matching action expert that outputs a 2.5 s horizon of acceleration and curvature controls, augmented with a soft visual mask applied to the expert's cross-attention. Compared to an identically trained baseline, the masked policy achieves comparable overall open-loop error while reducing error on left turns. In local closed-loop evaluation across the same 150 scenes (two rollouts per scene), the visual mask increases the mean scene score from 0.479 to 0.517 (paired difference +0.038, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.018, +0.093], wins/losses 37/26, sign test p = 0.21). Incorporating a rule-based automatic emergency braking (AEB) module at deployment further increases the mean score to 0.599 (+0.082, CI [+0.023, +0.143]) and reduces the mean number of scenes with at-fault collisions from 34.0 to 11.0.

llm.title_ja: カメラベースの緊急ブレーキを備えたGatedVLA：AlpaSim E2Eクローズドループチャレンジ技術報告書
llm.tldr_ja: 駆動事前学習済みVLAポリシーにソフトな視覚マスクを適用したレイヤー別フローマッチングアクションエキスパートを組み合わせ、緊急ブレーキモジュールを追加することで閉ループ性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: エンド端の自動運転において、VLAモデルのオープンループ誤差とクローズドループでの安全な走行性能を同時に高めること。
llm.method: Qwen-Drive-1.0-4Bとクロスアテンションにソフトな視覚マスクを適用したフローマッチングアクションエキスパートを組み合わせ、ルールベースの自動緊急ブレーキ（AEB）を統合する。
llm.result: 視覚マスクにより平均シーンスコアが0.479から0.517に向上し、AEBの追加によりスコアが0.599に向上し有責衝突シーン数が減少した。

2611.01659.title: HuG: Learning Humanoid Whole-Body Affordance-Aware Grasping with Active Perception
2611.01659.abstract: Acquiring objects in human environments is hard for humanoids: targets are partially occluded under egocentric viewpoints, and reaching them demands coordinated whole-body motion that keeps the target visible and reachable while the base stays stable. We present HuG, a framework for whole-body affordance-aware grasping with active perception that couples perception and action through a Perceive-Align-Grasp pipeline: belief-driven active perception resolves occlusion by treating viewpoint as an explicit decision variable; a point-cloud-conditioned affordance policy proposes whole-body grasps; and an affordance-aware alignment stage repositions the body to the most executable configuration. A key insight is that, on a floating base, kinematic validity is not enough: we curate training data with controller-in-the-loop dynamics simulation, rejecting 73% of kinematically valid grasps that would destabilize the deployment controller, so the policy learns kinodynamically feasible affordances. Trained entirely in simulation with zero real demonstrations, HuG attains 87.5% real-world success on a multi-level shelf task, generalizes to novel objects, and holds at least 73% success at every tested height. Beyond generalizing within its training distribution, the policy extrapolates spatially: at scale in simulation it succeeds at table heights well below any seen during training, indicating that kinodynamically filtered synthetic data grounds affordances in object geometry and whole-body feasibility rather than in memorized configurations.

llm.title_ja: HuG：能動知覚を用いたヒューマノイドの全身アフォーダンス認識把持の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 能動知覚によるオクルージョン解消、点群条件付きアフォーダンス方策、およびキノダイナミクスを考慮したアラインメントを統合したパイプライン「HuG」により、シミュレーション訓練のみでヒューマノイドのロバストな全身把持を実現した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイド環境において、ターゲットが部分的にオクルージョンされ、ベースの安定性を保ちながら可視性と到達可能性を維持する協調的な全身運動が要求されること。
llm.method: 視点を意思決定変数として扱う能動知覚、点群条件付きアフォーダンス方策、コントローラ内包型シミュレーションでフィルタリングされたデータによる訓練を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 実世界のマルチレベル棚タスクにおいて87.5%の成功率を達成し、新規物体へも汎化した。

2611.01645.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
2611.01645.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

llm.title_ja: UA-Depth：材料非依存の物体操作に向けた不確実性考慮型深度修復
llm.tldr_ja: 深度とピクセル単位の不確実性を反復的に共同洗練し、不確実性ゲート付き特徴を用いて信頼性の低い手掛かりを抑制する「UA-Depth」を提案し、透明・反射物体を含む多様なシーンで深度修復と下流タスクを改善した。
llm.problem: RGB-Dカメラが透明や反射面などの非ランベルト反射物体で穴やバイアスのある深度を生成し、不確実性を無視して一律に扱われていること。
llm.method: 深度とピクセル単位の不確実性を反復共同洗練し、凍結された深度基礎モデルを事前分布として初期化に活用し、MAD加重対数深度スケール正規化を適用する。
llm.result: 8つのゼロショットベンチマークにおいて代表的なベースラインの中で最良の平均順位を達成し、カテゴリ別6D姿勢推定と6D把持合成を改善した。

2611.01627.title: EgoMo3R: Joint Egocentric Motion and Scene Reconstruction
2611.01627.abstract: Understanding holistic 3D human motion and the surrounding environment from egocentric video is fundamental for applications in AR/VR and robotics. Although these tasks are inherently coupled, existing methods treat them separately. In particular, egocentric motion reconstruction methods typically assume access to metric, gravity-aligned camera trajectories from specialized inertial sensors. Recovering such trajectories from monocular egocentric video remains a significant challenge due to rapid head movements and motion blur. We present EgoMo3R, a joint optimization framework that simultaneously reconstructs 3D human motion and scene geometry from casual egocentric video. It leverages the robustness of low-level visuo-geometric primitives, including monocular depth, optical flow, and point tracks, integrated with a diffusion-based human motion prior via first-order optimization. We propose an alternating optimization scheme that establishes a synergistic feedback loop: scene reconstruction provides physical grounding and trajectory conditioning for the motion prior, while the motion prior regularizes the camera trajectory and anchors the scene in a metric, gravity-aligned world frame. We evaluate EgoMo3R on the highly dynamic sequences of the EgoExo4D and Nymeria datasets and show that it outperforms specialized baselines in both 3D scene reconstruction and egocentric motion estimation.

llm.title_ja: EgoMo3R：一人称視点モーションとシーン再構築の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼一人称視点ビデオから一人称視点の3D人間の動きとシーンジオメトリを同時に再構築するため、低レベル視覚幾何学的プリミティブと拡散ベースの人間モーション事前分布を交互最適化するフレームワーク「EgoMo3R」を提案した。
llm.problem: 一人称視点ビデオからの3D人間の動きと周囲環境の理解において、高速な頭部運動とモーションブラーによりメートル単位の重力整合カメラ軌道の復元が困難であること。
llm.method: 単眼深度、オプティカルフロー、点追跡などの低レベル視覚幾何学的プリミティブを、拡散ベースの人間モーション事前分布と第一種最適化により統合し、交互最適化を行う。
llm.result: EgoExo4DおよびNymeriaデータセットの高度に動的なシーケンスにおいて、専門特化したベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.01609.title: MagPillar: A Soft Magnetopillar Array Tactile Sensor for Robotic Surface Perception
2611.01609.abstract: Robotic surface exploration benefits from tactile interfaces that accommodate contact and capture variations in surface characteristics. Herein, we report MagPillar, a tactile sensor inspired by spider tactile hairs that combines a magnetic pillar array with three-axis Hall sensing. A full-array mechanical and magnetic-field model characterizes how pillar deformation affects the superposed fields measured across the array, providing a physical basis for interpreting its contact responses. The compliant pillar architecture translates contact with surface textures and geometric features into distinct magnetic response patterns. Then, in robotic surface perception experiments, spectral features and logistic regression distinguish six material surfaces with an offline accuracy of 99.34% under within-session temporally blocked cross-validation. Continuous scans over periodic protrusions produce amplitude and peak-spacing variations consistent with changes in surface geometry. These findings connect compliant contact mechanics with distributed magnetic sensing, paving a new path for material recognition and qualitative surface-profile perception.

llm.title_ja: MagPillar：ロボットの表面知覚に向けた柔らかいマグネトピラーアレイ触覚センサ
llm.tldr_ja: クモの触毛に着想を得た磁気ピラーアレイと3軸ホールセンシングを組み合わせた柔らかい触覚センサ「MagPillar」を開発し、接触変形に基づく表面材質の識別と幾何学的特徴の認識を実現した。
llm.problem: ロボットの表面探索において、接触を受け入れ表面特性の変化を捉える触覚インターフェースが必要であること。
llm.method: 磁気ピラーアレイと3軸ホールセンシングを組み合わせ、ピラー変形がアレイ全体の磁場に与える影響を物理モデルで解析して接触応答を解釈する。
llm.result: オフラインの交差検証において6種類の材質表面を99.34%の精度で識別し、周期的突起のスキャンで幾何学的変化に応じた振幅・ピーク間隔の変化を捉えた。

2611.01600.title: SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts
2611.01600.abstract: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.

llm.title_ja: SCOUT：オブジェクト中心型世界モデルのロールアウトを通じたオクルージョン下での計画
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクト中心のシーン表現と学習済み世界モデルに基づくモンテカルロ木探索（MCTS）を組み合わせることで、オクルージョンが存在する雑然とした環境での長期的なタスク計画とマニピュレーションを実現するフレームワーク「SCOUT」を提案した。
llm.problem: 雑然とした空間でマニピュレーションを行うロボットは、前景の物体がターゲットや自由空間を遮る部分的な視界から計画を行う必要があり、従来のリアクティブ方策や網羅的探索では対応が難しいこと。
llm.method: オブジェクト中心のシーン表現で隠れたジオメトリを再構築し、LLMが提案した構造化アクション候補を世界モデルを用いたMCTSで評価する。
llm.result: RevealおよびPlacementタスクにおいて、VLA方策や既存の3D世界モデルを大きく上回る性能を示し、実世界の棚環境でのマニピュレーションで有効性を検証した。

2611.01581.title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Exoskeleton Assistance Policies through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback
2611.01581.abstract: To reduce reliance on manual design and extensive parameter tuning, a framework for the autonomous evolution of exoskeleton assistance policies through human feedback is proposed. Assistance policies are autonomously generated as executable control code by an intelligent agent and evaluated in experiments with human participants. Subjective user feedback, movement performance, and muscle activation measurements are incorporated into policy assessment. Based on these assessments, policy deficiencies are autonomously identified and the control code is revised by the agent for subsequent trials. A closed loop of policy generation, human feedback, evaluation, and autonomous refinement is thereby established. The framework is evaluated using GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, and Kimi, and initial assistance performance and refinement outcomes are compared across models. Despite differences in initial performance, effective assistance is achieved with all four models after a single autonomous refinement iteration under the tested conditions. Across three tasks, biceps and triceps muscle activation levels are reduced by 29.4% and 35.2%, respectively, compared with those measured without an exoskeleton. However, limited adaptability to unexpected situations is observed, indicating that further improvements in robustness and safety are required.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループのフィードバックを通じた外骨格補助方策の再帰的自己改善
llm.tldr_ja: 知能エージェントが実行可能な制御コードとして補助方策を自動生成し、被験者実験からの主観的評価や筋活動の測定フィードバックを基に自律的にコードを修正・改善するクローズドループフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 外骨格の設計における手動調整の依存度を軽減し、人のフィードバックに基づいて補助方策を自律的に進化させること。
llm.method: エージェントが制御コードとして補助方策を生成し、人間のフィードバック、運動パフォーマンス、筋活動を評価に用いて方策の欠陥を自律的に修正する。
llm.result: 4つの異なる言語モデルを用いたテストで1回の自律的修正イテレーション後に効果的な補助が達成され、上腕二頭筋・三頭筋の活動がそれぞれ29.4%および35.2%減少した。
llm.limitation: 予期せぬ状況に対する適応性が限定的であり、ロバスト性と安全性のさらなる向上が必要であること。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンインザループ

2611.01565.title: Beyond Validation Loss: Coverage and Reliability Dynamics in Robot Policy Pretraining
2611.01565.abstract: In modern robot learning, generative robot policies are first pretrained through supervised learning from demonstrations, then refined through reinforcement learning, supervised finetuning, or other forms of posttraining. Yet conventional pretraining metrics, such as validation loss and average task success, provide an incomplete account of which policies support both effective direct deployment and subsequent posttraining. In this work, we study closed-loop pass@k, which evaluates the probability that k rollouts from the same initial condition attain at least one success. Thus, pass@1 measures mean task success; large-k pass@k measures whether success remains reachable under repeated sampling. Across a wide range of posttraining recipes, we show that large-k pass@k reveals posttraining differences not captured by pass@1. In particular, checkpoints with similar pass@1 but different large-k pass@k have different posttraining performance. Moreover, we show pass@k peaks at different checkpoints during supervised pretraining, revealing a coverage-reliability tradeoff over the course of training. Based on these observations, we propose two practical interventions: (1) a purely offline checkpoint-selection criterion that balances coverage and reliability without closed-loop evaluation, and (2) a generative data augmentation procedure that expands supervision beyond the finite demonstration set, preserving large-k pass@k while maintaining or improving pass@1 and raising the observed coverage-reliability Pareto frontier. Together, our results motivate evaluation, checkpoint selection, and training procedures that explicitly account for posttraining. Blog post, visualizations, and code are available at https://zhanyisun.github.io/robot-policy-learning-dynamics/.

llm.title_ja: 検証損失の先へ：ロボット方策事前学習におけるカバレッジと信頼性のダイナミクス
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模な成功確率評価指標（large-k pass@k）を用いることで、従来の検証損失やタスク成功率では捉えきれないロボット方策のポストトレーニング性能の差異を明らかにし、カバレッジと信頼性のトレードオフを改善する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の検証損失や平均タスク成功率などの事前学習指標では、直接的なデプロイとその後のポストトレーニングの双方を支える方策を十分に評価できないこと。
llm.method: 同一初期条件からのk回のロールアウトで少なくとも1回成功する確率を評価する「pass@k」を用いた分析と、オフラインのチェックポイント選択基準およびデータ拡張手順の提案。
llm.result: large-k pass@kがスーパービジョン事前学習中に異なるチェックポイントでピークを迎え、カバレッジと信頼性のトレードオフが存在することを明らかにした。

2611.01560.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
2611.01560.abstract: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.
2611.01560.hf_summary_en: Uni-robot-agent enables open-weight robot-use agents to surpass proprietary models in zero-shot manipulation and suggests joint development of four core capabilities for future training.

llm.title_ja: ロボット利用エージェントの民主化：オープンモデルによる統合ハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: オープンウェイトのロボット利用エージェント向け統合ハーネス「uni-robot-agent」を提案し、プロプライエタリモデルを凌駕するゼロショット操作性能と、将来の訓練に向けた4つのコア能力の重要性を示した。
llm.problem: ロボット利用エージェント（RUA）の研究が、フロンティアであるプロプライエタリモデルへの依存によってさらなる発展が制限されていること。
llm.method: オープンウェイトモデルを用いた、追加のトレーニングをサポートする統合ハーネス「uni-robot-agent」の構築と評価。
llm.result: Qwen3.8-Flash-Nextベースのエージェントがロボドジョースコアでプロプライエタリモデルの結果を上回り、19の実世界タスクで競争力のある性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボット利用エージェント

2611.01483.title: $TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering
2611.01483.abstract: Tactile sensing plays a crucial role in everyday human interaction. Consider inserting a plug into a tight socket, vision alone provides limited guidance during the final insertion stage, and we instead rely on both anticipated contact and realized tactile feedback to ajust the insertion motion. The same capability is equally important for robots, particularly in dexterous manipulation tasks. Yet many contemporary robot policies remain vision-dominant. This visual bias, compounded by limited tactile data and sparse contact events, can cause directly incorporated tactile signals to be ignored or even compromise the policy's pretrained capabilities, yielding degrading performance as observed in our experiments. We present $TF^2$-Steering, which refines actions via learned residual steering of the flow-matching action expert's velocity field, using a tactile mixture-of-experts architecture to integrate both tactile forecasts and real-time tactile feedback. Together with specific designed three stages training recipe, $TF^2$-Steering enables tactile signals to correct and, when necessary, redirect the flow-matching action-generation process, while building on the strong action-generation capacity of the vision-based foundation policy. Extensive experiments across six simulated and six real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of $TF^2$-Steering. It outperforms the strongest evaluated baselines by 10.7 percentage points in average simulation success rate and 9.1 percentage points in average real-world progress success rate. Project page: https://yiming-cc.github.io/tf2-steering/.

llm.title_ja: $TF^2$-Steering：速度場ステアリングを用いた触覚予測とフィードバックによるアクション洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 触覚混合エキスパートアーキテクチャを用いて触覚予測とリアルタイムフィードバックを統合し、フローマッチングアクション生成を残留ステアリングによって補正・誘導する「TF²-Steering」を提案した。
llm.problem: 多くの現代のロボット方策は視覚優位であり、限られた触覚データや疎な接触イベントによって触覚信号が無視されたり事前学習済み方策の性能を低下させたりすること。
llm.method: 触覚の予測と実時間フィードバックを統合する触覚混合エキスパートアーキテクチャを用い、フローマッチングの速度場を学習済み残差でステアリングする。
llm.result: シミュレーションで平均成功率が10.7パーセンテージポイント、実世界で9.1パーセンテージポイント向上し、既存ベースラインを上回った。

2611.01442.title: Dual Path Following for an Aerial Manipulator Under State and Input Constraints via Transverse Feedback Linearization
2611.01442.abstract: This paper studies dual path following for a quadrotor carrying a three-degree-of-freedom arm. The center of mass of the combined system must follow a vehicle path and the end effector must follow a second path, while the arm respects its joint limits and avoids its singular postures. The vehicle and the arm are mechanically coupled, so one controller must handle both paths. With the center of mass and the end-effector path coordinates as outputs, and a dynamic extension of the thrust, the system admits a normal form without internal dynamics. We characterize the states where this normal form fails. We formulate the transverse feedback linearizing controller as a quadratic program that relaxes only the speed of the end effector along its path and imposes safety and actuator limits as inequality constraints. The program reduces to a scalar problem with a closed-form solution. If it remains strictly feasible for all time, the feedback is locally Lipschitz, both paths are invariant and attractive, and every constraint holds. In the physics engine Drake, the controller resolves a conflict between the two speed references by slowing the end effector while both paths remain invariant. By contrast, a cascade with a safety filter leaves both paths. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/am_dual_pf-/

llm.title_ja: 状態および入力制約下におけるトランスバースフィードバック線形化を用いた空中マニピュレータのデュアルパス追従
llm.tldr_ja: 重心とエンドエフェクタの2つのパスを同時に追従させるクアドロータ・マニピュレータ向け制御手法を提案し、トランスバースフィードバック線形化に基づく二次計画法により制約を満たしつつ安定な追従を実現した。
llm.problem: 3自由度アームを搭載したクアドロータにおいて、システム全体の重心のパスとエンドエフェクタのパスを、機械的な結合や関節限界・特異姿勢を考慮しながら単一のコントローラで追従させること。
llm.method: 重心とエンドエフェクタのパス座標を出力とし、トランスバースフィードバック線形化に基づく二次計画法によりエンドエフェクタの速度のみを緩和して安全・アクチュエータ制約を課す。
llm.result: 物理エンジンDrakeを用いた検証において、2つの速度参照間の衝突をエンドエフェクタを減速させることで解決し、両方のパスが不変性を保つことが示された。
keywords_ja: フィードバック線形化

2611.01437.title: Adaptive Surface Cleaning under Uncertain Cleaning Response
2611.01437.abstract: Surface cleaning requires robots to adapt both where they clean and how they interact with contamination whose response to cleaning may vary spatially and remain unobservable prior to interaction. We formulate adaptive surface cleaning as a partially observable Markov decision process and propose a belief-aware planning framework that uses observed cleaning outcomes to update a latent local cleaning-response model and adapt subsequent cleaning motions, forces, and passes. Preliminary grid-world simulations demonstrate the resulting closed-loop planner adapting its spatial decomposition and cleaning actions as the surface evolves.

llm.title_ja: 不確実な清掃応答下における適応的表面清掃
llm.tldr_ja: 表面清掃を部分観測マルコフ決定過程として定式化し、観測された清掃結果を用いて局所的な清掃応答モデルを更新し、後続の清掃動作や力を適応させる信念認識型プランニングフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 表面清掃において、ロボットは清掃に対する汚染物質の応答が空間的に変動し事前には観測できない環境下で、清掃場所と相互作用方法を適応させる必要があること。
llm.method: 部分観測マルコフ決定過程（POMDP）として定式化し、観測された結果から潜在的な局所清掃応答モデルを更新して行動を適応させる信念認識型プランニング。
llm.result: グリッドワールドの予備シミュレーションにおいて、表面の変化に応じて空間分解と清掃行動を適応させる閉ループプランナーの動作が示された。
keywords_ja: 部分観測マルコフ決定過程

2611.01404.title: Serving Agentic Robot Fleets: Workload Characterization, KV-Cache Thrashing, and Admission Control
2611.01404.abstract: Agentic robots combine a vision-language brain, a tool-using harness, and a vision-language-action (VLA) policy. Serving a fleet of these agents introduces two coupled resource constraints: the brain repeatedly revisits long, growing key-value (KV) cache states, while the VLA executes action chunks under tight control deadlines. We characterize 80 LIBERO-PRO episodes generated by GPT-6-Astra, RPent, and pi0.5 (1,862 brain turns and 1,582 VLA inference chunks), profile both layers on H800 graphics processing units (GPUs), and replay the resulting agent programs on a vLLM serving engine. Brain contexts reach 215k tokens; the median Astra request takes 7.78 s, while the intervening environment-step gap is only 1.0 s. Under a 0.25 s action-chunk deadline, one VLA GPU meets the 1% starvation target for one robot; under a 1.0 s deadline, its measured capacity reaches at least 32. In sustained brain replay, increasing concurrency from 20 to 32 robots reduces throughput from about 2.4 to 0.6 requests/s as repetitive prefill displaces generation. A static active-episode cap restores 2.24-2.25 requests/s and raises completed trace-program throughput from 1.30 to 5.00-5.55 episodes/min. Our measurements expose the workload-dependent shift between action deadlines and brain KV residency, and establish practical principles for capacity planning and admission in sustained agentic robot fleets.

llm.title_ja: エージェント型ロボットフリートのサービング：ワークロード特性評価、KVキャッシュスラッシング、およびアドミッション制御
llm.tldr_ja: エージェント型ロボットフリートのサービングにおける脳のKVキャッシュ増大とVLAの制御レイテンシの競合を分析し、アドミッション制御とキャパシティプランニングの原理を確立した。
llm.problem: 脳の長期KVキャッシュ状態の再訪とVLAの厳格な制御期限という2つの結合したリソース制約。
llm.method: 80件のLIBERO-PROエピソードのプロファイリングとvLLMサービングエンジンでのリプレイ、および静的なアクティブエピソード上限の設定。
llm.result: 静的なエピソード上限の導入により、スループットが2.24-2.25リクエスト/秒に回復し、完了したトレースプログラムのスループットが向上した。

2611.01390.title: Same Path, Less Time: Training-Free Fast Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models under Inference Latency
2611.01390.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, yet deployed robots waste time in two ways that are independent of model capability: they halt while the next chunk is inferred, and they move at the speed of slow, cautious demonstrations. Existing remedies remove one loss each, and stacking them fails, because asynchrony and speed-up each change the correspondence between planned progress and executed motion. We present Path-preserving Time Scaling (PTS), a training-free execution layer for frozen action-chunking policies built on one principle: the robot's motion is a time reparameterization of a reference path, and the path changes only in response to new observations. A path layer decodes every replan deterministically in one step and enters it at the progress consumed during inference. A time layer sums the planned increments, keeps the arm at 1x while the gripper moves, and caps the rate by the actuator's linear range and by chunk feasibility under latency. We show that misaligned entry and stochastic sampling add a bias and a variance to the continuation error, and derive a break-even success rate that states when speeding up pays off. On LIBERO with two frozen VLAs under injected inference latency, PTS raises task throughput over the strongest deployable baseline by 33% for pi0.5 and 104% for SmolVLA while matching or improving the success rate, is best on all six model-suite combinations, and exceeds zero-latency 1x execution. Against asynchronous 1x execution with the same one-step decoder, the time layer alone adds 28% and 38%. On LIBERO-Dynamic it improves on stop-and-wait execution by 38% and is comparable to asynchronous 1x execution.
